652d7c0afebb11f3: KUALA LUMPUR: Sugar baby arrangements do not automatically constitute criminal conduct, but those involving coercion, exploitation or sexual services may cross legal boundaries, a criminologist has warned.

Speaking on this week's Beyond the Headlines, criminologist Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said authorities must assess the circumstances of each case, as financial assistance between consenting adults does not, by itself, amount to solicitation or prostitution.

She said describing payments as gifts or allowances did not automatically place such arrangements outside the law, adding that the nature of the exchange and the conduct involved were crucial in determining whether an offence had occurred.

Haezreena also warned that financial dependence could become a means of control, with seemingly consensual relationships escalating into manipulation, pressure to engage in unwanted sexual activities, blackmail or extortion.
Other warning signs include grooming, emotional manipulation and isolation, as well as threats to expose private messages or photographs when one party attempts to end the relationship.

She said universities should strengthen financial assistance, counselling services and confidential reporting mechanisms to help vulnerable students seek support without fear of humiliation or disciplinary action.
She added that policymakers and relevant agencies needed better evidence on the extent of exploitation linked to such arrangements to develop targeted prevention measures and ensure accountability.
Rather than treating all transactional relationships as exploitative, she said, efforts should focus on identifying coercion and abuse while ensuring those affected could access help.
More in the latest episode of NST's Beyond the Headlines on NST Online's YouTube channel.
* This episode was recorded on Oct 29.

fc57ce039bcc058c: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) will use its official party logo in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali.

Mohamed Azmin, who is also the party election director, said he had sent an official letter to the Election Commission (EC) last week regarding the confirmation of the party’s logo usage in the state election.

“We will use the Bersatu logo. I have sent a letter to the Election Commission and the use of the Bersatu logo has been approved by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin,” he said to reporters here yesterday.
He said this after officiating the Bersatu Candidate Announcement Ceremony for the Melaka State Election at the party’s main operations room in Baitul Tariq, Klebang, here last night.
Also present at the event was Bersatu vice-president Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin.
Commenting on the eight seats contested by Bersatu in the Melaka State Election, Mohamed Azmin said all those seats were seen as having the potential to be won by the party.

According to Mohamed Azmin, although Bersatu is expected to clash with the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates in the four contested seats, namely in Kelebang (PKR) as well as Gadek, Ayer Keroh and Pangkalan Batu (DAP), however, they leave it to the wisdom of the people of Melaka to make their choice.
“In the context of elections, overlap or clashes mean that the parties involved will compete, but we take the stance that this competition is a healthy competition in a democratic system.

“We will not practice ‘gutter politics’ or slander, we will offer party policies... we are a party that cares for the people, focusing on issues of the economy, growth and job creation,” he also said.

Earlier, at the event, Mohd Radzi announced that Bersatu will contest in eight State Assembly seats namely Lendu, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Pantai Kundor, Kelebang, Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh and Bemban. — Bernama
19b42b71bb0a7aa9: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has postponed announcing its candidate for one remaining state seat allocated to the coalition under an understanding with Barisan Nasional (BN) for the 16th Melaka state election.
Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the delay was due to several outstanding matters, not a lack of qualified candidates.

“We have one seat for which we have yet to announce a candidate, but this is not because we lack suitable candidates. There are matters that need to be resolved, which is why we did not announce the name tonight.
“We will settle all the seats by nomination day,” he told reporters at a press conference after PN's candidate announcement ceremony at Dewan Muallim Haji Abdul Wahid, Bukit Katil, here last night.
Asked whether the delay stemmed from disputes over seat allocations among coalition component parties, Ahmad Samsuri said this was not the case.
He also confirmed that the coalition had mutually agreed to allocate another seat, Bandar Hilir, to MCA.

“Insya-Allah, we are contesting to win. That is the most important thing, and I believe our machinery is working towards that goal. With this cooperation and understanding, I believe success is within our reach,” he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 for polling in the Melaka state election, with nomination on October 31 and early voting on November 10. — Bernama
2c3e1cc491fdcd25: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia slipped into negative territory on Friday after opening slightly higher, tracking weaker overnight sentiment on Wall Street amid disappointing technology earnings.
At 9.13 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 0.66 of a point, or 0.04 per cent, to 1,610.50 from Thursday's close of 1,611.16.
The benchmark index had opened 0.70 of a point higher at 1,611.86.
Across the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 265 to 107, while 265 counters were unchanged, 2,143 remained untraded and 66 were suspended.
Turnover stood at 291.30 million units worth RM95.01 million.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street closed mostly lower following weaker earnings from US technology giant Alphabet Inc, reigniting concerns over the substantial capital expenditure required for artificial intelligence (AI) investments.
"On the home front, we believe the benchmark index remains in consolidation mode, with fundamentally sound blue chips offering selective opportunities following the recent correction.
"Hence, for today, we envisage the benchmark index hovering within the 1,600-1,620 range," he told Bernama.

Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose two sen to RM10.02, while CIMB gained seven sen to RM6.96 and IHH Healthcare added four sen to RM7.89. Public Bank shed one sen to RM4.72, while Tenaga Nasional was unchanged at RM13.30.

In active trade, Zetrix AI and JAKS Resources shed one sen each to seven sen and 14 sen, respectively. GIIB Holdings fell 10.5 sen to 43.5 sen, while Ni Hsin and EWI Capital gained one sen each to 38 sen and 14.5 sen, respectively.

Country View topped the gainers, rising 14 sen to RM2.85, followed by Kein Hing, which added six sen to RM1.08. Genting Plantations gained five sen to RM5.10, while Lianson Fleet rose four sen to RM1.52.

Among the top losers, Malaysian Pacific Industries fell 60 sen to RM40.90, while UWC Bhd shed 20 sen to RM7.44. MN Holdings declined 12 sen to RM3.83, while Pentamaster Corporation lost nine sen to RM5.80.

On the index board, the FBM Emas Index fell 17.00 points to 12,038.89, while the FBM Top 100 Index shed 15.29 points to 11,835.67. The FBM Mid 70 Index declined 66.17 points to 17,417.95, the FBM Emas Shariah Index lost 32.73 points to 12,051.55, and the FBM ACE Index slipped 32.61 points to 5,414.55.

Sector-wise, the Energy Index increased 0.28 of a point to 844.64, the Financial Services Index jumped 18.69 points to 18,556.63, while the Plantation Index added 18.44 points to 8,655.34. The Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.36 of a point to 177.03.
02ec77745da79cab: TUMPAT, Oct 30 — Police have opened three investigation papers in relation to extreme comments on social media related to enforcement issues that are alleged to threaten public order and tarnish the image of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said a male suspect has been detained in relation to this case, whereas two other cases are under investigation and the suspects have been identified.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 504 of the Penal Code, Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“The police have never rejected criticism or reprimands aimed at improvement and safeguarding the public’s interest.

“However, action will be taken against statements that are insulting, defamatory, or extreme accusations that can disrupt public order,” he said at a press conference after patrolling the country’s waters at the Region Three Marine Police Force jetty, Pengkalan Kubor, here yesterday.
In related developments, he said that 42 individuals were detained in Kelantan this year for offences under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM).
Of that number, two individuals were detained for human trafficking offences, while the 40 others were involved in migrant smuggling offences.
Mohd Yusoff said that this number of arrests was compared to 59 individuals in 2025 and 51 in 2024.

He added that the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will continue to intensify enforcement efforts to combat the smuggling of undocumented migrants and curb the involvement of any parties in such syndicates.

Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff said that members of the public who receive threats from the illegal immigrant smuggling syndicate in Kelantan are urged to come forward and file a police report to enable an investigation to be conducted and action to be taken against the parties involved.
He said that reporting the incident to the authorities is more effective than merely spreading information or allegations through social media, which can expose the informant to further threats.
The public need not worry too much about coming forward to assist the investigation because witness protection mechanisms are available for cases that meet the criteria, including high-profile cases.
“It is better to report to the police so that we can conduct further investigations, identify the perpetrator and take action, including making arrests to resolve the issue,” he said.
He said that community cooperation is very important in efforts to combat smuggling activities using sea routes, especially in the Malaysia-Thailand border area.

In related developments, Mohd Yusoff said that a total of 4,873 immigrants were detained by various enforcement agencies in Kelantan from January to October this year, with 3,100 of them detained in districts bordering Thailand, including Kota Bharu.

He also said that Myanmar nationals recorded the highest number of arrests, with 1,977 people, followed by Bangladeshi (899), Indonesian (740), and Thais (more than 600), while the rest involved other nationalities, making a total of 26 nationalities involved in the arrests.

Mohd Yusoff added that the number of arrests this year also exceeded the record of 4,166 people for the entire year of 2025 and 3,689 people in 2024, thus showing that enforcement actions against the entry of immigrants continue to be intensified. — Bernama

4579298d0a405543: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian plantation companies could benefit from firmer crude palm oil (CPO) prices in 2027 as worsening drought conditions in Indonesia threaten to tighten regional supply.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the latest production outlook from Wilmar International Ltd had reinforced concerns over drought-related supply disruptions extending into next year.
Singapore-listed Wilmar is one of the world's largest oil palm plantation groups.
As at end-2025, the group had 234,334 hectares of planted oil palm estates, with about 66 per cent in Indonesia and another 25 per cent in East Malaysia.
The agribusiness group now expects fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production at its Indonesian estates to decline this year, reversing its earlier forecast of slight growth.
The revised outlook reflects worse-than-expected drought conditions in South Sumatra and parts of Kalimantan.
"Wilmar's weaker Indonesian palm oil output outlook reinforces concerns about drought-related supply risks extending into 2027, supporting our constructive crude palm oil view," CIMB Securities said.

The research firm said tighter supply could benefit Malaysian plantation companies with estates in Malaysia, although those with significant Indonesian exposure could also face weaker FFB yields next year.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Overweight" rating on the plantation sector, with Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK), SD Guthrie Bhd and IOI Corporation Bhd among its preferred picks.
It maintained "Buy" calls on all three companies, with target prices of RM24.32 for KLK, RM6.52 for SD Guthrie and RM5.03 for IOI Corporation.

However, the research firm cautioned that near-term CPO price gains could be limited by elevated Malaysian palm oil inventories, weak consumption and the possibility of improved sunflower oil supply from the Black Sea region.
It said a meaningful recovery in palm oil demand from Chinese buyers would depend on a sustained price discount against soybean oil.
8e56d08c83ae102a: NEW YORK: Wall Street's worries about the cost of the AI boom escalated after the market close on Thursday, as results from Amazon and Intel showed the infrastructure race is not only straining the tech industry but affecting consumers.

Surging data-center spending, as highlighted in Amazon's massive cash burn, has turned once debt-light tech giants into major borrowers, while price hikes are squeezing global demand for devices like smartphones and PCs.

Amazon forecast holiday-quarter sales below Wall Street expectations, a potential sign of growing pressure on consumers as inflation picks up, which also hit Intel's PC business, as a memory chip shortage has driven up its costs.

The AI spending spree is also eating into Big Tech's once-enviable cash flows. Alphabet and Meta both burned cash in the September quarter, while Microsoft, the only exception, joined their borrowing binge with a US$25 billion debt sale on Thursday.
The tech giants have deep pockets to sustain their spending, but investors have grown increasingly wary of smaller AI cloud firms borrowing heavily to deliver on enormous order backlogs.

Amazon's 7% after-hours slide was accompanied by losses of 5.8% to 6.7% in AI cloud stocks CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren. Alphabet, which closed regular trading down nearly 13%, fell another 1.5% after-hours.

The semiconductor index also sold off post-close after Intel blamed "near term headwinds across the PC industry." The index had already dropped 1.4% during the regular session due to Alphabet's messy earnings report.
Shares of PC makers HP and Dell sank 8% and 6.8%.

"The revenues missed due to lower PC demand and forward guidance also disappointed. As Google learned today, earnings matter," said Kim Caughey Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners LLC. Google parent Alphabet dropped 13% on Thursday.
Intel, whose shares were down 18%, also said a factory explosion in Israel caused a two-week shutdown and would cost it roughly US$600 million in lost revenue over two quarters.
"Overall semiconductor weakness after hours is primarily a function of Intel guide and negative sentiment spillover," said Michael James, equity sales trader at Rosenblatt Securities.

Some analysts said Intel's problems in the PC sector, an area of technology that does not garner the same scrutiny on Wall Street as the AI buildout, do not seem to necessarily mean big problems for other chipmakers that operate more prominently in AI.

Nevertheless, investors in the less-active post-market trade chose to shoot first and ask questions later. AMD dropped 4% and Broadcom fell 2%. Among the biggest losers in the volatile session was the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull, which offers investors three times the daily performance of the SOX and was off 9%.

The SOX has been one of 2026's standout performers, rising more than 60% as shortages of chips and equipment needed for the AI buildout drive up prices and profits at firms ranging from giant Nvidia and memory chip firm Micron to Marvell Technology.

But the momentum of that trade has been tested over the past month by tightening financing terms. That has kept some expected IPOs on the sidelines and put some highly leveraged AI infrastructure firms under pressure. The SOX has declined 13% since hitting its recent high in October and is off 21% from its all-time high in June.

"I think Intel was seen as this unicorn within the tech sector because it was seen as being weaker compared to Nvidia and AMD," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
"It just had this miraculous rise, and you got a lot of retail money into it, and some of that money is easy come, easy go."
232426b43f480fee: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is deeply wary of the unity between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the upcoming Melaka state election, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man claimed.

“We know the challenge posed by AI is enormous today. Various media will be used in all kinds of ways.
“The aim is to create doubt among party supporters, question decisions and candidates, dig up secrets and even look for things that do not exist to tarnish our candidates,” he said.
He added that all party members should accept the candidates chosen by the party, saying they were the best choices for the people.
He said every candidate had undergone a vetting process at the Syura Ulama Council level.
“PAS is well known as a party whose members are obedient and abide by the party’s decisions.
“Once the party has made a decision, whether you like it or not, you must obey and comply, as long as you are not instructed to do something sinful,” he said.

3bf27b9a6e08cd5d: KUALA LUMPUR: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday it had frozen US$3 billion in crypto assets as it investigated a potential security breach, with stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether also freezing related assets.
"Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said, without providing further details about the incident.
The market impact of the potential hack, which could be the largest-ever cryptocurrency heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis, was felt immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.
Bitcoin fell about 2 per cent to a six-week low of US$77,646, while ether dropped around 2 per cent to a two-month low of US$2,238.76.
BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, fell more than 8 per cent over the past 24 hours to US$694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.
Crypto exchange Coinbase Global fell 4.8 per cent, while shares of bitcoin buyer Strategy dropped nearly 6 per cent in extended US trading.

Binance said the amount frozen could increase as it worked with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company, said in a post on X that the incident "looked like a hack".

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has more than 335 million registered users globally and held about US$160 billion in assets under custody, according to its 2024 annual report.
BINANCE HAS SECURE ASSET FUND
Binance operates a secure asset fund for users, according to its website. The reserve is held entirely in bitcoin and is intended to protect user assets in the event of security breaches.

"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them," said Bernardo Brites, chief executive officer of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.
"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."
Tether said it had frozen nearly US$1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than US$800 million.
Binance said it was conducting security checks and would resume withdrawals once the issue was fully resolved. It added that user funds remained safe and its teams were reviewing the incident.
The exchange also temporarily suspended trading on its Binance Alpha platform as a precaution.

World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack.
Yi said US$27 million in stablecoins and about US$2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Cryptocurrency firm Ripple also froze roughly US$200 million in funds, Yi said.

Jack McDonald, senior vice-president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds while coordinating with relevant parties.
INCIDENT ADDS TO STRING OF CRYPTO THEFTS

Miguel Morel, chief executive officer of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been stolen from Binance by an unknown actor, although the exact cause had not been confirmed.
Morel said the incident began at around 4.30pm EDT (2030 GMT) and appeared to be ongoing.
The incident adds to a string of cryptocurrency thefts. Attackers stole US$2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks last year, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said about US$350 million in crypto assets had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.
Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.
Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.
Coinbase said it was also unaffected and was monitoring the situation.

In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

b19f97ac921aa7f3: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — Damage to a 750-millimetre concrete pipe has been identified as the cause of a sinkhole on Mayang Pasir Highway in Bayan Baru near here, with repair works expected to be completed by November 7.
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) Sdn Bhd was carrying out repairs in stages to ensure safety at the site.

“The sinkhole has been temporarily covered with a steel plate, and safety measures in the area have been strengthened. IWK is also diverting the water flow and pumping water out of the sinkhole in preparation for the next phase of repairs,” he said in a statement last night.
He said sheet piling works to stabilise the ground were scheduled to begin tomorrow, ahead of excavation works.
The affected road will remain closed until repairs are completed. Motorists have been advised to use alternative routes via Lebuh Mayang Pasir, Jalan Mahsuri and Lorong Mayang Pasir 1.

7b18bb23360d6585: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar for the 10th consecutive trading day yesterday reflecting sustained positive sentiment towards the local currency at the start of trading.
At 8 am, the ringgit edged up to 4.0570/0625 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0575/0620.
The local currency was trading near a seven-week high, following a previous opening level of 4.0560 recorded on Sept 9, 2026.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.33 per cent to 101.854 points.

He said the decline came despite better-than-expected US gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026) and a higher personal consumption expenditure (PCE) inflation rate in September.
Mohd Afzanizam said the two-year and 10-year US Treasury yields also fell by 10 and eight basis points to 4.60 per cent and 4.94 per cent, respectively.
“Hence, we believe the market is pricing in the possibility that the Federal Reserve (Fed) might change its direction on monetary policy.

“As such, the ringgit is likely to maintain its positive trend in the near term, given the limited scope for further Fed monetary tightening. The ringgit-US dollar pair could therefore hover between RM4.05 and RM4.07 today,” he told Bernama.
Against other major currencies, the ringgit traded lower at the opening.
It weakened against the British pound to 5.4275/4348 from 5.4009/4069 at Thursday’s close, and slipped against the euro to 4.5365/5427 from 4.5176/5226.
It also edged lower against the Japanese yen to 2.5707/5743 from 2.5685/5715 previously.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit traded mixed.
It was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 223.6/224.0 from 223.7/224.0 at Thursday’s close, and remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.35/6.36.
Meanwhile, the ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1700/1746 from 3.1665/1702 at Thursday’s close, and slipped against the Thai baht to 12.0279/0513 from 12.0165/0345. — Bernama
af7c8345022a4928: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the government to exempt existing foreign workers from mandatory Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributions and a proposed RM300 monthly minimum wage increase, saying the measures would impose additional costs on local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

The DAP lawmaker said he had told Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that employers, including MSMEs, were opposed to the mandatory contributions and the increase in minimum wages for existing foreign workers.
He claimed Anwar had been given misleading information suggesting that employers had begun accepting the requirement for a 2 per cent EPF contribution for foreign workers.
In a written parliamentary reply on October 22, Anwar said 78,129 employers had contributed to the EPF for 1,754,460 non-Malaysian workers since the mandatory scheme was introduced in October 2025.
Of these employers, 67,194, or 86 per cent, were SMEs, which Anwar said indicated that the policy was beginning to gain acceptance and was being implemented by employers.
However, Lim said those responsible for SME affairs had failed to inform the prime minister of the actual opposition among businesses to the policy.
He said the mandatory EPF contributions should apply only to newly recruited foreign workers, as the requirement was not included in existing employment contracts.
Lim argued that imposing the contributions on existing foreign workers would increase employers’ labour costs unexpectedly and affect their financial position.

He cited the Malaysian Employers Federation’s estimate in 2025 that annual spending on foreign workers’ wages exceeded RM70 billion, saying the financial implications for the national economy could be substantial.

Lim also objected to raising the monthly minimum wage for existing foreign workers by RM300, from RM1,700 to RM2,000, saying this would have an even greater financial impact on employers and contradict existing salary agreements.

He questioned the government’s reliance on International Labour Organisation (ILO) principles against discrimination between foreign and local workers to justify extending the same benefits to foreign employees.
Lim asked why foreign domestic workers were exempt from the mandatory 2 per cent EPF contribution despite also being foreign workers.

He also cited Singapore’s decision to exclude foreign workers from contributions to its Central Provident Fund, which is similar to Malaysia’s EPF, from January 1, 2003, questioning why the ILO had taken no action over the arrangement.

On minimum wages, Lim questioned why Malaysian workers employed by companies with annual sales of less than RM50 million were not required to comply with the additional RM300 increase, while domestic workers were also exempt.
He asked whether these exemptions did not amount to discrimination.
Lim said he had conveyed the concerns and dissatisfaction of MSMEs to Anwar during a meeting at the Parliament administrative block on Tuesday, October 27.
He urged the government to prioritise local employers by exempting existing foreign workers from mandatory EPF contributions and the additional RM300 minimum wage increase.
7a2d55159b350882: MUNICH: Bayern Munich host long-time foes Borussia Dortmund on Saturday after a rollercoaster week punctuated by coach Vincent Kompany's hospitalisation and Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph.
Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, a mainstay in Bayern's midfield, has missed three games on compassionate leave due to the sudden death of his father.
Luis Diaz, Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala and Aleksander Pavlovic have all battled injury for the defending champions.
Bayern's issues have pushed what is usually the biggest match of the Bundesliga season into the background.
The only unbeaten teams after seven matchdays, Bayern and Dortmund sit level on points, with Saturday's hosts ahead on goal difference.
Dortmund coach Niko Kovac said Thursday his side, who have also battled injury issues this season, were "getting closer" to Bayern.
But Bayern's main task will be to shut out the noise and focus on the game.
'Highs and the lows'
After showing signs of illness in Bayern's 6-1 thumping of RB Leipzig, Kompany returned to the dugout for last week's 2-2 home draw with Arsenal, but collapsed on the training pitch two days later.
Later diagnosed with meningeal irritation, the Belgian was released after five days in hospital on Wednesday, but Bayern said it will likely be "weeks, not days" until he returns to work.
Charged with carrying Kompany's clipboard, assistant Aaron Danks hoped the waves of emotion would galvanise the side.
"You've seen the full extremes of life in the last week. The joys and highs for Harry, and the lows of some of the things we've had to go through in the last seven days," Danks said Tuesday.
"Internally we have to find a balance... In these moments, you understand the human being is the most important thing...
"These moments do bring you closer, because they're challenging moments, but to get through these moments we've had to rely on our team spirit and our togetherness."
At the other end of the emotional spectrum is Kane, who received the game's highest individual honour on Monday.
Kane said Wednesday it had been a "crazy week" for himself and the club, adding: "I get quite embarrassed by it, but I know it's a big deal.
"It's been a whirlwind 48 hours, it's nice to be back here and feel at home again."
Kane became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 and just the fifth ever to win the Ballon d'Or, with some calling for the England captain to be knighted.
"I certainly wouldn't say no, that's for sure," Kane said. "But it'll feel a bit weird everyone calling me 'sir', so we'll just keep it as Harry.
"If it happens, it'll be incredible and something I'll be massively proud of, but I don't want to get too carried away."
World Cup winner Lothar Matthaeus, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1990 with Inter Milan, said Kane would respond well to the recognition.
"When you win the Ballon d'Or, the story is not over. It has to motivate you," Matthaeus told AFP and other media on Wednesday.
"For me, for sure it was an honour to win, but football is a team sport. This Ballon d'Or is not only for Kane, it's also for Bayern Munich."
e694547c0ca7fb60: SEREMBAN, Oct 30 — A 74-year-old man was killed after the Perodua Myvi he was driving was swept away by floodwaters while travelling along a road near a drain beside Sungai Kampung Kundur Hulu here in Rembau last night.

a9db27a7e01989c2: MELAKA: Former Pengkalan Batu assemblyman Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee is unfazed by the nicknames he earned during his previous tenure, including "YB Beliau" and the "pig-shooting assemblyman", as he prepares to return to public service.
The 60-year-old Bersatu candidate said the labels were simply part of his experience as a people's representative, particularly his willingness to go to the ground and address residents' problems.
He said when elected in 2018, he had always strived to serve the community to the best of his ability, recognising that the mandate and opportunity came from the people.
"Look at the labels I received. Which assemblyman would dare to go out and shoot wild boars? I was even called a pig, but to me, it was just a nickname.
"An elected representative must be courageous and work with sincerity to solve the people's problems. That was what I did before, and I intend to do even better this time," he said.
He was speaking after Bersatu's candidate announcement at the party's main operations room at Baitul Tariq in Klebang last night.

Norhizam, who is also Bersatu Hang Tuah Jaya deputy division chief, said that despite turning 60, he wanted to focus on residents' basic needs, particularly flash floods caused by drainage and clogged drains, which he claimed had yet to be comprehensively addressed.
He also highlighted road conditions, education and the need to help small entrepreneurs obtain business licences and suitable premises.

He pledged to push for fairer opportunities for small G1 and G2-class contractors through open tenders, instead of large-scale concession-based project awards that make it difficult for smaller contractors to secure work.
"Small contractors are struggling to earn a living, and we will do our best to help them secure suitable work opportunities," he said.

On the contest for the seat, the former Melaka state executive councillor for agriculture, entrepreneur development, cooperatives and agro-based industries said his previous experience as the area's assemblyman and ties with residents would help him connect with voters.
He said he was prepared to sacrifice sleep, having previously managed with only about three hours a night to focus on serving the public.
"People say I am already 60, but my spirit is still going strong," he said.
Norhizam won the Pengkalan Batu seat in the 2018 14th General Election (GE14) under the DAP ticket with 9,227 votes.
After leaving DAP, he contested as an independent candidate in the 2021 Melaka election but lost to Barisan Nasional's Datuk Kalsom Noordin, securing 1,218 votes.

9e8a2275addacea4: PETALING JAYA: Syarikat Malaysia digalak memanfaatkan tumpuan China terhadap teknologi bernilai tinggi bagi tempoh 2026 hingga 2030, khususnya dalam kecerdasan buatan (AI), ekonomi digital dan teknologi hijau.

Kaunselor Menteri dan Pesuruhjaya Perdagangan Perbadanan Pembangunan Perdagangan Luar Malaysia (Matrade) di Kedutaan Malaysia di Beijing Niqman Rafaee M Sahar berkata keutamaan di bawah Rancangan Lima Tahun Ke-15 China membuka ruang kepada syarikat tempatan untuk menjalin kerjasama dalam pembangunan teknologi, inovasi industri dan pengkomersialan penyelidikan.
Katanya, peluang itu termasuk penyumberan strategik, perkongsian kepakaran dan pemindahan teknologi yang boleh membantu meningkatkan keupayaan industri Malaysia.
"Keutamaan itu turut meliputi penggunaan teknologi dalam sektor industri dan peningkatan produktiviti melalui pendigitalan, di samping peralihan kepada pembangunan hijau,” katanya.
Beliau berkata demikian ketika menerima kunjungan Timbalan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif VFive Group Sdn Bhd Amir Junaidi Amerrudin di pejabat Matrade di Beijing.

Niqman berkata Matrade turut menggalakkan syarikat Malaysia melihat peluang di bandar peringkat kedua, ketiga dan keempat di China, selain pasaran utama seperti Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou dan Shenzhen.
Menurutnya, langkah itu dapat mempelbagaikan pasaran eksport dan membuka akses kepada sektor industri serta teknologi sedang berkembang.

Matrade, katanya, terus membantu syarikat Malaysia memasuki pasaran China menerusi promosi eksport, pemadanan perniagaan, pembangunan hubungan perdagangan serta khidmat nasihat mengenai keperluan dan pematuhan eksport.

Sementara itu, Pengasas dan Pengarah Urusan VFive Group Syafiq Abdullah, berkata syarikat itu sedang meneroka kerjasama dengan pemain teknologi China dalam perubatan digital, sistem AI, jentera pertanian pintar dan teknologi pembinaan moden.
Katanya, tumpuan diberikan kepada teknologi yang praktikal dan sesuai dengan keperluan industri Malaysia, termasuk dari segi kos pelaksanaan serta kesesuaian operasi tempatan.

Dalam sektor pertanian, katanya, penggunaan jentera pintar dan AI boleh meningkatkan kecekapan menerusi automasi, pemantauan tanaman berasaskan data serta penggunaan input pertanian dengan lebih tepat.
"VFive juga sedang mengenal pasti peluang perkongsian kepakaran dan pemindahan teknologi bagi menyokong pembangunan industri tempatan," katanya.
1fbb625650734644: PETALING JAYA: One day, she was going about her life. Then, in an instant, everything changed. The hair salon owner, in her early 50s, suffered a major stroke, leaving her unable to speak or respond.

By the time she reached the hospital, the 4.5-hour window for clot-busting medication had passed. Doctors removed the blockage through a mechanical thrombectomy, but she remained critically ill in intensive care, reliant on a feeding tube and a tracheostomy.
Her story is a sobering reminder that a stroke can upend an ordinary life without warning. And according to neurologist Hoo Fan Kee, it is no longer a condition associated only with old age.
“People tend to think that a stroke is something that happens only to the elderly, but that is not true,” Hoo told FMT Lifestyle.
“We have about 50,000 new stroke cases in Malaysia. The number has been increasing every year, and we've been seeing more and more younger patients ... it is quite alarming.”

The National Stroke Registry recorded that 45.9% of patients between 2017 and 2024 were younger than 60, while 12.7% were below 45. Hoo, president of the Malaysia Stroke Council, pointed to obesity, sedentary lifestyles and metabolic problems as contributors.
The registry also found that 71% of registered stroke patients had high blood pressure and 40% had diabetes. Smoking and vaping are additional concerns, Hoo said.
While a stroke can strike suddenly, its risk factors often develop over years. Many, however, can be addressed through everyday choices.
“Weight management is one of the keys,” Hoo, said, recommending a healthy body mass index of 18.5 to 22.9 for Asian populations.
“A healthy diet is the way to go. Many studies have proven that the Mediterranean diet is very effective for prevention.”
To that end, Hoo advised eating more fibre, vegetables, fruits, whole grains, beans and nuts, alongside healthy oils such as olive oil.
“Our diet is quite salty, very sweet and oily,” he said. “We should reduce salt to less than five grams per day.”

Hoo recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise weekly, resistance training twice a week and seven to nine hours of sleep nightly. Regular health screening for blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol is also important.

But prevention is only part of the equation. Recognising the warning signs and acting quickly can make a critical difference. Hoo urges the public to remember BE FAST: Balance, Eyesight, Face, Arm, Speech and Time.

“The golden hour is only 4.5 hours,” he said, referring to the standard window for eligible patients to receive clot-busting medication. Some patients with large clots may qualify for mechanical thrombectomy, depending on their condition and brain imaging.

Yet, getting treatment quickly is not always straightforward. Hoo cited Malaysia’s ratio of just 0.43 neurologists per 100,000 people. “To tackle this problem, we have to empower internal medicine and allow emergency physicians to get involved in acute stroke treatment,” he said.

Thrombectomy services remain concentrated in the Klang Valley. Data from 2022 and 2023 showed only 3% of Malaysian ischaemic stroke patients received clot-busting treatment, compared with 12% in Thailand.
Recovery can be a long journey, too. Hoo said Malaysia lacks sufficient rehabilitation centres and beds, leaving families to shoulder much of the burden.
“The golden period for rehabilitation - especially the first month, and up to nine months - is very important,” he said. “We do see a lot of improvement with intensive rehabilitation.”

Families must learn new caregiving skills while adjusting to sudden changes in their lives. The hair salon owner’s husband's determination helped her regain some independence, but her journey also demonstrates that stroke care must continue beyond the hospital emergency department.
“About six months after the stroke, she could walk slowly, and her husband took her to a park each evening. She could also shake hands and recognise the nurses who cared for her,” shared Hoo.
For him, the message is clear: “Prevention is the way to go, not until they get a stroke. If they do suffer a stroke, recognise the BE FAST symptoms and go to the right hospital as soon as possible.”
7a5cabdbc29837f2: PETALING JAYA: Actual benefits delivered to the people should be the yardstick by which Sabah’s development is measured, not the size of allocations or number of projects completed, analysts say.
They said there should also be performance audits to determine such progress or failures.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri, an analyst at business consultancy Global Asia Consulting, said it was imperative that substantial allocations be matched by effective implementation.
Furthermore, there must be accountability for delays and failures in achieving objectives, he said.
“The real question is not how much money is allocated, but how many of the people’s problems have been resolved,” he told FMT.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak affairs) Mustapha Sakmud said recently that requests for increased allocations should translate into faster and more effective implementation of projects.
Under Budget 2027, Sabah was allocated RM18.7 billion and Sarawak RM16.2 billion, each an increase of RM1.1 billion from the previous year.
Zaharuddin proposed that reports for every project be published every six months, detailing actual budget already disbursed, physical progress and the number of beneficiaries.
“Don’t just report that a project is 90% complete when the people have yet to benefit from it,” he said.

Lai Wei Sieng of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) said roads, water and electricity supplies should be prioritised, as inadequate basic infrastructure raised both the cost of living and cost of doing business.
He said allocations should take into account poverty levels, geographical size and infrastructure shortfalls, with the more underserved rural areas receiving higher per capita funding.

Lai also proposed a public portal displaying project locations, contract values, contractors, implementing agencies, progress and funds disbursed, while residents should be allowed to verify whether completed facilities were functioning properly.
Who is responsible for project delays?
Lai said performance audits should identify the causes of project delays, including contractor failures, procurement problems or overlapping federal and state jurisdictions.
He proposed that the national audit department lead the audits, while the implementation coordination unit in the Prime Minister’s Department monitors project progress on site.

“Delays caused by approval issues should be recorded in the performance assessments of the officials responsible, while funds should be disbursed based on physical progress verified by independent engineers,” he said.
Zaharuddin said that for every major project, the person responsible for its implementation and progress must be made available to answer queries from the public.
He said contractors who failed to deliver should face penalties and be blacklisted in accordance with existing regulations.
Furthermore, he said, the federal and state governments should not blame each other when projects fail to be implemented.
“The federal government cannot use state autonomy as an excuse to shirk responsibility. Likewise, the state government cannot use federal failures to shield its own shortcomings,” he added.
816d8bbca62f037c: PETALING JAYA: Kejayaan pembangunan Sabah perlu diukur berdasarkan manfaat sebenar kepada rakyat, bukan jumlah peruntukan atau peratus projek siap, kata penganalisis.
Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri daripada Global Asia Consulting berkata, peruntukan besar perlu disusuli pelaksanaan berkesan dan akauntabiliti terhadap projek lewat atau gagal mencapai matlamat.
“Persoalan sebenar bukan berapa banyak wang diperuntukkan, tetapi berapa banyak masalah rakyat berjaya diselesaikan,” katanya kepada FMT.

Beliau mengulas seruan Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Hal Ehwal Sabah dan Sarawak), Mustapha Sakmud, supaya peningkatan peruntukan diterjemahkan kepada pelaksanaan projek lebih pantas dan berkesan.
Di bawah Belanjawan 2027, Sabah menerima peruntukan RM18.7 bilion manakala Sarawak RM16.2 bilion, masing-masing meningkat RM1.1 bilion berbanding tahun sebelumnya.

Zaharuddin mencadangkan laporan pencapaian diterbitkan setiap enam bulan, merangkumi kos sebenar, kemajuan fizikal dan jumlah penerima manfaat. “Jangan sekadar melaporkan projek sudah 90% siap sedangkan rakyat masih tidak menikmati manfaatnya,” katanya.
Lai Wei Sieng daripada Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) berkata, jalan raya, bekalan air dan elektrik perlu diutamakan kerana kekurangan kemudahan asas meningkatkan kos sara hidup dan perniagaan.
Katanya, pengagihan dana perlu mengambil kira kemiskinan, keluasan kawasan dan kekurangan infrastruktur, dengan kawasan pedalaman yang paling ketinggalan diberi peruntukan per kapita lebih tinggi.

Beliau mencadangkan portal awam memaparkan lokasi projek, nilai kontrak, kontraktor, agensi pelaksana, kemajuan dan penyaluran dana, manakala penduduk pula perlu diberi ruang mengesahkan sama ada kemudahan yang siap benar-benar berfungsi.
Lai berkata, audit prestasi perlu mengenal pasti punca kelewatan, termasuk kegagalan kontraktor, masalah perolehan atau pertindihan bidang kuasa Persekutuan dan negeri.
Beliau juga mencadangkan Jabatan Audit Negara mengetuai audit, manakala Unit Penyelarasan Pelaksanaan di Jabatan Perdana Menteri memantau kemajuan projek di tapak.

“Kelewatan akibat masalah kelulusan perlu direkodkan dalam penilaian prestasi pegawai bertanggungjawab, sementara penyaluran dana dibuat berdasarkan kemajuan fizikal disahkan jurutera bebas,” katanya.

Zaharuddin pula mahu setiap projek utama mempunyai pegawai bertanggungjawab yang dikenal pasti secara terbuka. Kontraktor yang gagal perlu dikenakan penalti dan boleh disenarai hitam mengikut peraturan.
Katanya, kerajaan persekutuan dan negeri tidak boleh saling menyalahkan apabila projek gagal dilaksanakan.

“Kerajaan persekutuan tidak boleh menjadikan autonomi negeri sebagai alasan melepaskan tanggungjawab. Kerajaan negeri pula tidak boleh menggunakan kegagalan persekutuan sebagai perlindungan daripada kelemahan sendiri,” katanya.
94ea8ec3df481ffd: KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd is poised for stronger earnings in the final quarter of 2026 after its nine-month performance exceeded market expectations.
The stronger-than-expected results prompted Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) to raise its earnings forecasts for the semiconductor equipment and materials manufacturer.
PublicInvest said the group's core net profit surged 73 per cent year-on-year to RM152 million in the first nine months of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY26).
The earnings accounted for 78.4 per cent of the research firm's full-year forecast and 90 per cent of consensus estimates.
Following the results, PublicInvest raised its FY26 to FY28 earnings forecasts by about 10 per cent and maintained its "Outperform" call, with a higher target price of RM9.45.
The research firm expects earnings momentum to continue into the fourth quarter, supported by stronger demand for semiconductor materials and a recovery in equipment deliveries.
Mi Technovation's semiconductor materials business remained its main earnings contributor, generating more than RM100 million in earnings during the nine-month period.

The division is expected to gain further momentum in the fourth quarter, driven by demand from high-performance computing and memory customers, alongside steady orders from the mobility and wearables segment.

Meanwhile, its semiconductor equipment business is expected to record double-digit revenue growth for the full year despite a 2.2 per cent decline in the first nine months, implying a substantial recovery in fourth-quarter deliveries.

For the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, Mi Technovation's core net profit jumped 82.2 per cent to RM66.5 million from a year earlier, supported by stronger contributions from its semiconductor materials business.
Revenue grew 30 per cent year-on-year, driven mainly by semiconductor materials sales, which doubled to RM154 million.

The increase was supported by stronger demand for solder spheres from the mobility and wearables segment, sustained orders from high-performance computing and memory customers, and a gradual recovery in the automotive and renewable energy segments.
The semiconductor materials division's earnings tripled to RM55.1 million from RM18 million a year earlier.
PublicInvest attributed the improvement to higher capacity utilisation of more than 85 per cent at its Tainan plant in Taiwan and stronger sales of higher-margin patented solder spheres.
Better performance at its Ningbo plant in China also contributed to the growth.
The division recorded a net profit margin of 28.1 per cent for the first nine months of FY26.

In contrast, revenue from the semiconductor equipment business fell 18.7 per cent year-on-year to RM100.4 million in the third quarter, likely due to lower equipment deliveries, although the average selling price per machine increased.
PublicInvest expects deliveries of Mi Series die-sorting and smart-binning equipment, as well as Si Series test handlers, to pick up in the fourth quarter.
Meanwhile, Mi Technovation's newer semiconductor technologies and vehicle technologies businesses remained loss-making, recording combined losses of RM24.5 million in the first nine months.
PublicInvest said commercial production of the group's Vanda 1 power management chip had been delayed until the third quarter of 2027 due to prolonged wafer fabrication lead times.
Development of Vanda 2, however, remained on track.
The group's electric powertrain systems business was also ramping up operations, with commercialisation expected to support significant growth in 2027.

379a7fe3097402d3: ROCK HILL: President Donald Trump's administration filed a revised lawsuit on Thursday seeking to block Alaska's election results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses and, according to a person familiar with the matter, issued more than 40 subpoenas and document requests in its probe.

The revised complaint by the US Justice Department cited a New York Times report that Democratic operatives recruited another candidate named Sullivan who could siphon votes from the incumbent. The Justice Department said the effort was intended to mislead voters and help elect Democratic candidate Mary Peltola.

The suit raises the prospect of a messy fight over a contest that could determine US Senate control in next Tuesday's midterm elections. Republicans hold a 53-47 majority, while Democrats need a net gain of four seats.

“They orchestrated his sham campaign for the purpose of misleading Alaskan voters and getting Peltola elected,” lawyers for the Justice Department wrote in their amended complaint, referring to a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who is on the ballot without a party affiliation.

Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy also called for a state investigation into the allegation and said in an interview with News Nation that any finding of illegality "may in fact impact whether someone is seated in the US Senate."
Peltola's campaign did not immediately respond to the amended complaint but has previously said it had "no involvement with either Sullivan campaign.”

The Times reported on Wednesday that Peltola aides worked with campaign lawyers and staff at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee to recruit two candidates who could siphon votes from the incumbent Republican Sullivan, including Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
Peltola’s former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, who was fired in August, told the Times that Peltola was aware of the effort.
The DSCC has denied involvement and accused Republicans of propping up candidates of their own in other races. Reuters was unable to independently verify the Times report.
Daniel J. Sullivan has previously denied in interviews with US news outlets that his aim is to cause confusion or divert votes from Dan S. Sullivan.

Trump, who for years has sowed doubts about the fairness of US elections, had pushed the Justice Department to bring the Alaska case even before the Times report, seeking to preemptively block Alaska from certifying Peltola, a former congresswoman, if she were to win the election.
Trump told reporters earlier on Thursday: "It's hard to believe that she could even be allowed to run. Frankly, I don't know how you can allow somebody like that to run. It's so unfair.
35f1dfd2bfaa7a5c: TEHRAN, Oct 30 — Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s armed forces said yesterday a day after the US military said it cleared key routes through the waterway.

“Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz,” Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement.
Iran’s army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait, after hitting mines while “operating in a restricted and dangerous area”.
The initial three vessels had “switched off all their radar and navigation systems” and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.
It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.
British maritime agency UKMTO, meanwhile, said it had received a report of a vessel on fire about 25 nautical miles (46 kilometres) northeast of Khasab, Oman, in the Hormuz strait.

Earlier, UKMTO reported two other incidents in the area: a dhow that caught fire and sank following a maritime security incident, and a tanker struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

In recent weeks, Iran has reported multiple vessels striking sea mines, prompting US Central Command (CENTCOM), which runs military operations in the region, to reaffirm on social media its insistence that all mines in “primary transit routes” have been cleared.
Hossein Mohebi, the spokesman for the IRGC challenged the claim, saying on X: “Prove your Hormuz mine-clearing claim with independent evidence, not statements!”
Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait. On Sunday CENTCOM said it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran considers ships using the southern corridor near the Omani coast unauthorised.

In their statement on Thursday, the Guards said “the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM’s delusions on social media”.
The IRGC also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone, in a separate statement.
“The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz,” the statement said. — AFP
befd885e5b14f6e7: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to making public the full report of a special committee that investigated allegations of share ownership involving former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki, subject to legal considerations.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said disclosure would be considered if necessary.

She said any decision must take into account existing legal provisions, particularly those governing personal data protection, the confidentiality of investigation documents, asset declaration records and the interests of relevant parties.

"Any announcement will be made by the Chief Secretary to the Government's Office, as stated in its March 31 media statement, should there be any official developments or decisions that warrant public disclosure.

"The issue of ownership and asset declarations, including Azam's shareholding, has been examined by the Special Investigation Committee established on Feb 13. The same question was also raised on June 25.

"The committee has completed its investigation independently, transparently and professionally, and its findings have been presented to the Cabinet," she said in a written parliamentary reply published on the parliament website today.

She was responding to Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who asked about the committee's findings on allegations concerning Azam's shareholding, any action to be taken against him and whether the government was prepared to make the report public.
fbeb0c49a0db4b68: NEW YORK: Wall Street's concerns over the cost of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom escalated after the market closed on Thursday, as results from Amazon and Intel showed that the infrastructure race was not only straining the technology industry but also affecting consumers.

Surging data centre spending, highlighted by Amazon's massive cash burn, has turned once debt-light technology giants into major borrowers, while price increases are squeezing global demand for devices such as smartphones and personal computers (PCs).

Amazon forecast holiday-quarter sales below Wall Street expectations, potentially signalling growing pressure on consumers as inflation picks up. This also affected Intel's PC business, as a memory chip shortage drove up its costs.

The AI spending spree is also eating into the once-enviable cash flows of major technology companies. Alphabet and Meta both burned cash in the September quarter, while Microsoft, the only exception, joined their borrowing spree with a US$25 billion debt sale on Thursday.
The technology giants have deep pockets to sustain their spending, but investors have grown increasingly wary of smaller AI cloud firms borrowing heavily to meet enormous order backlogs.

Amazon's shares fell 7 per cent in after-hours trading, accompanied by losses of between 5.8 and 6.7 per cent in AI cloud stocks CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren. Alphabet, which closed regular trading nearly 13 per cent lower, fell another 1.5 per cent after hours.

The semiconductor index also fell after the market closed after Intel cited "near-term headwinds across the PC industry". The index had already dropped 1.4 per cent during the regular session following Alphabet's disappointing earnings report.
Shares of PC makers HP and Dell fell 8 per cent and 6.8 per cent, respectively.

"The revenues missed due to lower PC demand and forward guidance also disappointed. As Google learned today, earnings matter," said Kim Caughey Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners LLC.
Alphabet, Google's parent company, fell 13 per cent on Thursday.
INTEL FACTORY SHUTDOWN
Intel, whose shares fell 18 per cent, also said a factory explosion in Israel had caused a two-week shutdown and would cost it about US$600 million in lost revenue over two quarters.
"Overall semiconductor weakness after hours is primarily a function of Intel guide and negative sentiment spillover," said Michael James, equity sales trader at Rosenblatt Securities.

Some analysts said Intel's problems in the PC sector, an area of technology that does not attract the same scrutiny on Wall Street as the AI buildout, did not necessarily point to major problems for other chipmakers with greater exposure to AI.
Nevertheless, investors in the less-active after-hours market appeared to react first and ask questions later. AMD fell 4 per cent and Broadcom declined 2 per cent.

Among the biggest losers in the volatile session was the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull ETF, which offers investors three times the daily performance of the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), and fell 9 per cent.

The SOX has been one of 2026's standout performers, rising more than 60 per cent as shortages of chips and equipment needed for the AI buildout drove up prices and profits at companies ranging from Nvidia and memory chipmaker Micron to Marvell Technology.

However, the momentum of the trade has been tested over the past month by tighter financing conditions. This has kept some anticipated initial public offerings (IPOs) on the sidelines and put some highly leveraged AI infrastructure firms under pressure.
The SOX has declined 13 per cent since hitting its recent high in October and is down 21 per cent from its all-time high in June.

"I think Intel was seen as this unicorn within the tech sector because it was seen as being weaker compared to Nvidia and AMD," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
"It just had this miraculous rise, and you got a lot of retail money into it, and some of that money is easy come, easy go."

f13565538b3485ed: PETALING JAYA: The police should focus on threats to students instead of taking over schools’ responsibility to address truancy, academics say.

Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia’s Effendi Ewan Matore said monitoring students’ attendance, investigating the cause of their absenteeism and counselling them should remain the responsibility of schools and the social welfare department.
He said the police should focus on educating students about the law, road safety and the dangers of drugs, as well as tackling external threats such as drug syndicates and gangsterism.
Effendi said police lacked the pedagogical training, social work expertise and policy tools needed to address the root causes of truancy such as poverty, learning difficulties and family problems.
"The police's involvement should not extend to monitoring the personal behaviour of ordinary students or compiling security profiles on them," he told FMT.

He was commenting on Kuala Lumpur police chief Fadil Marsus’s statement that police would track and profile about 10% of students in the capital who frequently played truant or had dropped out of school.
Fadil said the initiative was aimed at identifying the reasons for their absenteeism and helping them return to school.

Universiti Malaya’s Ungku Aziz Centre for Development Studies director, Suhaiza Hanim Zailani, said profiling was important to identify the reasons for absenteeism and determine the appropriate intervention.
She said students who skipped school should not automatically be viewed as potential offenders but as individuals who might need help.
"Police involvement can be useful when there are issues such as gang activity, substance abuse or other crimes affecting students," she said.
However, cases of truancy that do not involve such threats should be handled by education authorities, in collaboration with parents, counsellors and welfare agencies, she added.

Suhaiza said students might skip school because of financial difficulties, transport problems, family caregiving responsibilities, pressure to work, bullying or difficulties keeping up with their studies.
She said simply returning students to school without addressing the reasons for their absence would be only a temporary solution.

Suhaiza also warned that an approach which placed too much emphasis on police involvement could make students feel ashamed, fearful or cause them to be labelled as offenders, pushing them further away from school.

She stressed that students’ privacy must be protected if the police profile them, ensuring that the information gathered is used to support the students rather than create police records that could affect their future.
e368973183732f01: LIVERPOOL, Oct 30 — David Moyes pointedly praised Everton’s “really good values” after Jack Grealish was dropped for breaching club discipline prior to yesterday’s 3-1 win over Newcastle in the League Cup.
Grealish reportedly skipped training ahead of the fourth round tie and was left out of the Everton squad at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
The on-loan Manchester City winger had missed Everton’s defeat at Arsenal in the Premier League tomorrow due to illness.
Everton boss Moyes refused to give further details on Grealish’s absence against Newcastle, but backed the move to leave him out.
“It was a club decision. I support the decision. It’s something I don’t really want to speak too much about,” he said.

Asked about the response of his players on a night when the controversy could have been a distraction, Moyes’s answer suggested frustration with Grealish, who has repeatedly been criticised for his off-field behaviour.
England international Grealish fell out of favour at City after several late-night incidents and reports of after-hours drinking.
“I think the one thing about Everton and what they’ve got is they’ve got really good values behind it,” Moyes said.
“All the players stand up to the values, accept the values that we put out there, what we want from them on the pitch and off the pitch.
“And from that point of view I think the players have done a brilliant job tonight, they really did.”
Everton took control of the game in the first half with goals from James Garner and Hayden Hackney before Thierno Barry ended any doubt in the 69th minute.
Dan Burn scored a late goal for Newcastle but Everton eased through to face fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the quarter-finals in December.
Fleetwood stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday, but Everton will fancy their chances of making the semi-finals of a competition they have never won.
Everton have not lifted a major trophy since the 1995 FA Cup.
“I think the minute you use the word quarter-finals then you start to think, ‘this sounds good’,” Moyes said.
“I think we’re pleased that we’ve been able to get to this stage of the competition. If we can keep it going great, obviously.” — AFP
a13de07f1bb077d9: JERUSALEM: Prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a parliamentary majority, according to final results from Israel's general election released early Friday.
Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest single faction with 27 seats.
The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats.

The results from the Central Elections Committee also confirmed a dramatic breakthrough by Arab groupings Raam and the United Arab List, which together won 19 seats and could emerge as kingmakers in coalition talks.
The two parties were targeted by unproven election-fraud allegations circulated by Netanyahu's camp on Thursday.
Politicians and media reports claimed the parties were suspected of receiving Qatari funds to finance vote-buying.
The Arab parties and Qatar denied the allegations, while Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of seeking to "delegitimise" the election results.

Israel's Shin Bet domestic security agency said it was investigating suspected irregularities but added it was not intended to "cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner".
Without directly referring to the allegations against the Arab parties, the electoral commission said Thursday that some information that had circulated was entirely unfounded.
The investigation is continuing alongside the process being conducted by the Central Elections Committee. It will have no impact on the final results to be submitted to the president, it said.

The final results will be formally presented on Wednesday to President Isaac Herzog, who will then begin consultations with party leaders before tasking one of them with trying to form a government, the commission said.
The absence of a majority bloc points to potentially difficult coalition negotiations that could last for weeks.
If no government can be formed, Israel could face another election, as it has several times in the past.
67c4596114735c97: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is studying the need to improve existing legal provisions to address the issue of abandoned vehicles.

Its minister, Nga Kor Ming, said the joint initiative with the Transport Ministry aims to clarify powers and expedite enforcement and disposal processes while safeguarding the rights of vehicle owners.

The approach, he said, aims to shift the management of abandoned vehicles from a purely enforcement model to a comprehensive solution balancing legal authority, public rights, and owners' social responsibility.
"The ministry, in cooperation with the Transport Ministry, is also improving approaches through the use of various legal instruments that can be considered.
"This includes the Road Transport Act 1987, as well as introducing a more systematic voluntary disposal method to encourage owners to legally dispose of obsolete vehicles.
"The ministry is also improving the Guidelines for the Management of Abandoned Vehicles in Local Authority Operational Areas introduced in 2020.

"This aims to streamline procedures for tracking, removing, storing, and disposing of abandoned vehicles based on available powers under relevant laws, including the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament portal today.
He was responding to a question from Jimmy Puah (PH-Tebrau) on the ministry's plans to draft or amend existing laws to tackle abandoned vehicles nationwide.

Nga said the new guidelines are expected to be implemented by local authorities in the peninsula before the end of this year, while implementation in Sabah and Sarawak will be coordinated with the respective authorities according to applicable legal frameworks.

"The government stresses that the approach to managing abandoned vehicles is not merely issuing guidelines, but involves a comprehensive action framework based on good governance, field evidence, inter-agency coordination, and practical work process improvements for local authorities to implement.

"The government is confident that with the support of all parties, including the Transport Ministry and the police, the issue of abandoned vehicles can be addressed more effectively and holistically," he said.
4f503f69adf56fb3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government plans to reform federal development expenditure by moving away from a historical spending-based approach towards a model that prioritises equity and efficiency to narrow regional productivity gaps.
The Economy Ministry said the main focus was to trim the productivity gap between less-developed states and the national average.
“Annual increases in allocations under Budget 2027 do not necessarily mean that states receiving smaller allocations are underperforming compared with more developed states.
“Instead, these states may be more capable of diversifying their local economies by leveraging existing resources,” the ministry stated in a reply to the Dewan Rakyat today.

The ministry was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar (PN-Kemaman) on targets to narrow regional productivity gaps and mechanisms for allocating development funds based on the needs of states and their people.
The Economy Ministry said structural economic imbalances between states posed a threat to national competitiveness.
“If left unaddressed, regions lagging in production capacity will continue to widen the country’s productivity gap.

“Therefore, federal development allocations must serve as a key fiscal stimulus to address infrastructure deficits, technology gaps and labour market weaknesses in less-developed states, towards sustainable regional economic convergence,” it said. — Bernama
7fc9af4c5a95b838: KUALA LUMPUR: Gold prices eased in early Asian trade on Friday after falling more than one per cent in the previous session, as persistent US inflation fuelled expectations of further Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes, weighing on bullion.
Spot gold fell 0.4 per cent to US$4,006.06 an ounce by 0036 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.3 per cent to US$4,018.50.
Bullion was headed for a modest weekly gain but remained on track for a second consecutive monthly decline.
US inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for petrol and other goods, supporting economists' expectations of a Fed interest rate increase in December.
Traders are now pricing in about a 75 per cent chance of a rate hike in December, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

The European Central Bank (ECB) left interest rates unchanged in a widely anticipated move on Thursday but clearly signalled another hike in December, warning that high and rising energy costs were fuelling inflation risks.
ECB president Christine Lagarde will step down from her role on Feb 7, the central bank said.

Annual core inflation in Japan's capital exceeded the central bank's two per cent target by a wide margin in October, data showed on Friday, highlighting mounting price pressures and strengthening the case for further interest rate hikes.

The London Metal Exchange is seeking to turn metal held in its Hong Kong warehouses into digital assets that can be used for financing, a move linked to the territory's five-year plan to expand its commodities hub, three people familiar with the matter said.
Spot silver fell one per cent to US$51.87 an ounce, platinum was steady at US$1,488.00, while palladium declined 0.5 per cent to US$1,000.75.
All three metals were headed for weekly and monthly declines.
