9965617d9f55e165: MELBOURNE, Oct 30 — Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson lost a bid to overturn her convictions and had a harsher sentence imposed yesterday failing to prove she was wrongfully jailed for killing three people with a poisoned lunch.
Patterson was found guilty last year of murdering her husband’s parents and elderly aunt, deliberately lacing their beef Wellington meal with highly toxic death cap mushrooms.
The 52-year-old maintained her triple murder convictions were a “miscarriage of justice”, urging the Court of Appeal in Victoria state to either set her free or have the case heard again.
The court found the killings were “carefully planned and deliberate”, and there were insufficient grounds to try the case again.
“This offending was extraordinarily cold and calculated,” judge Stephen McLeish said.
“It stands to be denounced in the strongest terms.”
Patterson has also been convicted of the attempted murder of her husband’s uncle, a small-town local pastor who survived after weeks in hospital.
The court not only threw out Patterson’s appeal, it also found that her original jail sentence did not match the gravity of her crimes.
Patterson was initially eligible to apply for release after 33 years.
The court ruled that she should not be eligible for parole, meaning Patterson is likely to die in prison.
Patterson did not front the trial in person, instead watching proceedings via video link from a maximum security prison on the outskirts of Melbourne.
Her lawyers had alleged a litany of irregularities in the trial, including an “oppressive” cross-examination and unfair decisions on the admission of evidence.
Manifestly inadequate
Prosecutors argued that the non-parole period of 33 years imposed by the judge was “manifestly inadequate”.
They said the judge erred in finding there was a substantial chance Patterson would be held in solitary confinement for years to come, and this “infected” his decision on parole.
Patterson’s trial last year drew podcasters, film crews and true crime fans to a courthouse in the rural town of Morwell, a sedate hamlet in Victoria better known for its prize-winning roses.
Audiences from New York to New Delhi followed every twist of what many now simply call the “mushroom murders”.
The motive of the killings remains a mystery.

A 12-person jury found Patterson guilty in July last year of murdering her husband Simon’s parents, Don and Gail Patterson, as well as his aunt, Heather Wilkinson, at her home in the Victorian farming village of Leongatha.
She was also found guilty of attempting to murder Heather’s husband Ian, a pastor who fell gravely ill but eventually recovered. — AFP
cca232455bc07f0c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government is prioritising the Rural Roads Programme (JALB) project financing with the total allocation for 2026 rising to RM3.1 billion from the original allocation of RM2.11 billion, according to the Finance Ministry (MoF).

Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the nearly RM1 billion in additional allocation comprises the additional RM500 million for the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) and the earlier Notice of Change (NOC) worth RM491 million made by KKDW.

In his winding-up speech on the policy stage of the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027), he said the additional allocation was approved to ensure that the JALB projects could continue and contractors are paid.

Amir Hamzah said the approval, granted through the Expenditure Exceeding Allocation Authorisation Letter (SKB), was issued in stages, with RM300 million approved on September 1, 2026, and RM200 million on September 21, 2026.
“This allocation was still insufficient to settle existing (KKDW) commitments,” he noted.
Amir Hamzah said the additional funds channeled through the SKB mean development expenditure savings from other ministries.

Among the ministries are the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry; Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry; Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry; Agriculture and Food Security Ministry; Transport Ministry; Housing and Local Government Ministry; and Economy Ministry.
Amir Hamzah said the actual expenditure for JALB projects from 2018 to 2022 amounted to RM3.72 billion, while actual expenditure and allocations for the 2023-2027 period reached RM11 billion.

Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said applications for and approvals of NOCs must be completed before any new expenditure or commitments are undertaken, while any issuance of a new letter of acceptance (SST) should also be supported by sufficient allocations.
“On this basis, MoF requested KKDW on September 10, 2026, to defer the issuance of a new SST for JALB.
“Therefore, any claim that MoF cancelled the projects is untrue. MoF only requested that KKDW defer the issuance of a new SST until the existing arrears have been settled,” Amir Hamzah said.
He added that every additional allocation for JALB through reallocation reduces the fiscal space available to fund other priorities.

He said Budget 2027 brings together the strengths of the government, investment institutions, companies, banks, employers and the public based on their respective roles, whereby the collaboration expands the country’s capability to provide jobs, facilities and economic opportunities.

He said the RM50.2 billion in additional investments detailed in Budget 2027 comprises RM25 billion from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion from public-private partnerships, and RM14.2 billion from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies.
“Each component has its own funding sources, mandate and approval process,” he added. — Bernama
c794072f1e2c8251: LAHORE, Pakistan: Pavan Rathnayake's brilliant century went in vain as England stopped Sri Lanka from chasing a big 387 target, winning the dead rubber by 55 runs in Lahore on Thursday.
On the same day last week, Rathnayake scored an epic 130 in Sri Lanka's 430-run chase in Rawalpindi but this time his 77-ball 118 was not enough as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 331 in 45.1 overs.
England opener Ben Duckett had earlier smashed his highest ODI score of 167 to propel England to 386-5.
With 87 needed in the last ten overs Sri Lanka were on course for another upset victory but hopes vanished when spinner Liam Dawson dismissed Rathnayake caught off a miscued sweep in the 45th over.
Dawson finished with career best figures of 4-49, while Sonny Baker finished with 2-75.
Besides Rathnayake's third ODI hundred, skipper Kusal Mendis chipped in with a 71-ball 89 with five sixes and eight boundaries to keep Sri Lanka in the hunt.
Despite the loss Sri Lanka can take heart for Saturday's final against Pakistan – also in Lahore – with sloppy England departing with just one win in four games.
Rathnayake, who hit 15 boundaries and a six, added 80 for the third wicket off just 59 balls with Mendis to keep England at bay.
Mendis had earlier added 84 for the second wicket with Avishka Fernando, who scored a quickfire 48.
Rathnayake kept the fight with a 72-run stand for the fifth wicket with Janith Liyanage (30) but Baker broke the stand to bring England back in the game
England captain Harry Broo was relieved.
"The way we finished the game off, we've learned a lot from the game when they chased 430," said Brook. "That's really good. I wasn't getting nervy, to be honest.
"We haven't had the series we wanted, we'd have liked to be in the final on Saturday. The lads are taking a lot of confidence."
Mendis showed confidence for the final.
"We have batted well, so not to worry about the final and I am sure we will be up to the task come Saturday," said Mendis.
Duckett's 132-ball knock included 24 boundaries, anchoring the innings along with Tom Banton's 74 runs after England were put in to bat.
Duckett, whose previous highest was 165 against Australia in the Champions Trophy at the same venue last year, put on 163 for the opening wicket with Banton.
Banton's 75-ball knock had two sixes and eight boundaries.
Duckett added another rapid 107 off just 75 balls for the second wicket with Harry Brook, with skipper Brook hitting two sixes and three fours in his 34-ball 44.
Duckett finally fell to a miscued scoop off Eshan Malinga in the 42nd over.
Jordan Cox, with 43 runs, Will Jacks's 30 and Sam Curran, who was 21 not out, helped England add 92 runs in the last ten overs.
Pacer Asitha Fernando chipped in with 2-63 but fellow pacer Malinga's only wicket cost 101 runs. — AFP

e9bef8f38acbe39e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed Transport Minister Anthony Loke to urgently address overcrowding on train services, warning that the problem could disrupt the daily routines of commuters.
The directive followed a complaint by a Threads user identified as siti.anisahj, who highlighted overcrowding at train stations in a post last night, according to a report by Berita Harian.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he had also instructed Rapid KL to look into the problem and ensure a swift solution.
“This (train overcrowding) happens frequently and it certainly disrupts the daily routines of the wider public.
“We (the government) must be more attentive and take action,” the Tambun MP said.
The prime minister’s response attracted widespread attention, garnering more than 25,000 likes, nearly 300 comments and about 1,500 reposts.
In her earlier post, siti.anisahj shared several photographs showing the crowded conditions faced by train commuters, particularly in the capital, on a daily basis.

“Assalamualaikum @anwaribrahim_my. Could we have more train carriages, please? It's like this every day... driving means getting stuck in traffic, while taking the train means it's packed,” she wrote.
On October 12, KLIA Ekspres and KLIA Transit services were reportedly disrupted following two cable theft incidents within several hours along the airport rail corridor.
The incidents forced passengers to endure longer journeys and changes to train schedules.
The theft involved about 180 metres of signalling cables, comprising two sections of 90 metres each, between Putrajaya and Cyberjaya Station and Salak Tinggi Station, near the 44km marker.
Earlier, on October 8, the Kajang MRT Line experienced overcrowding at Bukit Bintang Station, with the situation lasting about three hours due to an increase in passenger numbers.
The congestion was also believed to have significantly affected commuters at other train stations, including Bangsar LRT Station, where many passengers were left stranded.
ff3cbf91c298d19b: TEHERAN: Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said on Thursday, a day after the US military said it had cleared key routes through the waterway.

"Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said in a statement.
Later on Thursday, Iran's army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait after hitting mines while "operating in a restricted and dangerous area".
The initial three vessels had "switched off all their radar and navigation systems" and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.
It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.
British maritime agency UKMTO, meanwhile, said late on Thursday that it had received a report of a vessel on fire about 25 nautical miles (46km) northeast of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz.

Earlier, UKMTO reported two other incidents in the area: a dhow that caught fire and sank following a maritime security incident, and a tanker struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

In recent weeks, Iran has reported multiple vessels striking sea mines, prompting US Central Command (Centcom), which oversees military operations in the region, to reaffirm on social media its claim that all mines in "primary transit routes" had been cleared.
On Thursday, Hossein Mohebi, the IRGC spokesman, challenged the claim, saying on X: "Prove your Hormuz mine-clearing claim with independent evidence, not statements!"
Since the outbreak of the war on Feb 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

The United States has responded by imposing a blockade on Iranian ports and helping tankers travel through the strait. On Sunday, Centcom said it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran considers ships using the southern corridor near the Omani coast unauthorised.

In their statement on Thursday, the Guards said "the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to Centcom's delusions on social media".
The IRGC also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone in a separate statement.
"The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz," the statement said.
d79290b17de94a80: LONDON, Oct 30 — Michael Carrick has been granted a stay of execution but will the beleaguered Manchester United manager survive a vital trip to Chelsea?
Arsenal face a significant test of their Premier League title defence at Liverpool, while Manchester City meet Brighton for the second time in four days.
AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of this weekend’s action:
Carrick clings on
With Manchester United fans on stand-by for news of Michael Carrick’s sacking this week, an unexpected show of patience has given the under-fire boss a new lease of life.

When Carrick was pictured driving into United’s Carrington training base on Monday—just 24 hours after a miserable 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth—it was widely expected he would be dismissed within hours.
Instead, United’s hierarchy sprang a major surprise by keeping Carrick, for now at least.
“I totally get the position. I understand the responsibilities. So, I really don’t need any assurances from anyone in that regard,” Carrick said of his future.
Whether Carrick can avoid becoming the third manager to be sacked by United powerbroker Ratcliffe since he purchased a minority stake in the club in 2024 remains in doubt.
United have been in miserable form and sit just one point above the relegation zone ahead of Saturday’s trip to fifth-placed Chelsea.
Without a victory in eight games in all competitions and off to their worst league start in 40 years, United must beat Chelsea to help Carrick stave off the axe.

But with captain Bruno Fernandes dropped last weekend after criticising Carrick’s tactics and defender Lisandro Martinez fined for blasting the club’s transfer policy, Carrick’s side are far from united.
Odegaard urges Arsenal to bounce back

Humiliated by one of the most chastening defeats in their club’s glittering history, Arsenal have a chance to erase the embarrassment of their League Cup loss at Fleetwood when they face title rivals Liverpool on Sunday.
Mikel Arteta’s side were left shell-shocked by their penalty shoot-out exit against fourth tier minnows Fleetwood following a dismal display in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw.

The Premier League champions were so far below their best that it was hard to believe this was the same team that stormed to the title last term and looked hungry to retain the crown in the opening weeks of this season.

A victory at Anfield would restore Arsenal’s belief and captain Martin Odegaard called on his team-mates to show their character against fourth-placed Liverpool, who can move within three points of the Gunners if they win this weekend’s marquee match-up.
“Obviously, the way we’ve played was not on the level. We need to do much, much better than we did,” Odegaard said.
“We can’t feel sorry for ourselves. We need to move on, we have a big game at the weekend, so bouncing back is all we can do now.”
Man City braced for Brighton rematch
Enzo Maresca has warned his Manchester City stars they will face a “brilliant” Brighton side fuelled by a desire to avenge their League Cup exit.
City twice came from behind to force a 2-2 draw against Brighton before winning a penalty shoot-out in the League Cup last 16 at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday.
City boss Maresca is a big fan of Fabian Hurzeler’s third-placed team and he is well aware of the danger they pose to the Premier League leaders in the rematch in Manchester tomorrow
“They are in a brilliant moment. They are winning games, they are scoring many goals every game,” Maresca said.
“I’ve watched all their Premier League games since we started, and they always go front foot, man to man. They’re going to be exactly the same tomorrow.” — AFP
b8624abb58daa6ad: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Bursa Malaysia Bhd to help more Malaysian companies grow into regional champions, saying too many promising businesses remain small for too long.
“I would like to see more mid-tier companies grow, list and become regional champions. Too many good companies stay small for too long.

“Bursa has a role in helping them take that next step. If it succeeds, we should see more Malaysian businesses grow, more good jobs created and more Malaysians holding a stake in the country’s progress,” he said in his keynote address at Bursa Malaysia’s 50th anniversary celebration yesterday.

Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, Bursa Malaysia chairman Tan Sri Abdul Farid Alias, Bursa Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Fad’l Mohamed and Securities Commission Malaysia chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi were also present.
Anwar added that the growth of Malaysian businesses could create more jobs and allow more Malaysians to share in the country’s progress.
He also stressed the importance of trust and fairness in the capital market, saying companies seeking investment from Malaysians must deal with them honestly.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said Malaysia’s market would face a changing global environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, technological change and the energy transition.

“The market has been through hard years. Financial crises and the pandemic tested companies, investors and regulators alike. Through each of them, the capital market kept doing its job. It kept investment flowing and helped the economy recover,” he added.
Anwar also urged Malaysian companies to move up the value chain in areas including semiconductors, advanced manufacturing and digital technology to compete confidently abroad.
The Prime Minister said the government had also put a great deal of effort into governance and fiscal discipline, as well as making Malaysia a more attractive place to invest.

“The results are showing. In the first half of this year, Malaysia recorded RM218.5 billion in approved investments. Under the Madani Economy, we are aiming to raise the ceiling of what our economy can achieve while raising the floor of our people’s living standards,” Anwar said. — Bernama
b908e28c5a396fc0: CAPE TOWN: Josh Inglis scored a second test century to help Australia to a 100-run first innings lead against South Africa at Newlands on Thursday, having only been told he would play in the decisive third test when he arrived at the ground on the first morning.
Inglis matched the 102 he scored against Sri Lanka on his test debut last year as he batted superbly with Alex Carey (80) to put Australia in command of the match.
Leeds-born Inglis, 31, came into the side when experienced batter Steve Smith pulled out on the morning of the first day with a neck injury.

"It wasn't ideal preparation (for the game), but Steve had been dealing with his neck issue for a while, so in my mind I was always preparing to play, just in case," Inglis told reporters. "He came down to the ground early, had a hit and didn't feel comfortable enough to play. I found out I was in the team once we got to the ground."
South Africa scored 329 in their first innings and Australia managed 429 in reply, led largely by Inglis' 102.
"When I got out there, I realised it was a really good wicket, so the most important thing was making sure we got a lead," he said.
"I'm still a bit disappointed we didn't get more runs this morning. If Kez (Carey) and I could have added another 50, that would have been really nice.
"We knew how good the wicket was and felt we needed a big total."

South Africa finished the day on 140 for four in their second innings, only 40 runs ahead with six wickets remaining. Australia grabbed the key wickets of Marques Ackerman (62) and Temba Bavuma (35) late in the final session.

"It was really satisfying. I thought we controlled the tempo well in that last session," Inglis said. "They put together a good partnership and were batting well, but they weren't really getting away from us.
"Gaz (spinner Nathan Lyon) bowled brilliantly and looked threatening the whole time. When you work hard for a couple of hours and finally get the rewards right at the end, it's really satisfying."
Inglis said chasing anything over 200 could be tricky batting last.
"I'm not sure of a total (to chase). You don't want them getting too many more than maybe 200 or so (ahead)," he added. — REUTERS

4dfe625bb04fb7dd: TEHRAN: Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said Thursday, a day after the US military said it cleared key routes through the waterway.

"Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement.
Later Thursday, Iran's army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait, after hitting mines while "operating in a restricted and dangerous area".
The initial three vessels had "switched off all their radar and navigation systems" and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.
It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.
British maritime agency UKMTO, meanwhile, said late Thursday it had received a report of a vessel on fire about 25 nautical miles (46km) northeast of Khasab, Oman, in the Hormuz strait.

Earlier, UKMTO reported two other incidents in the area: a dhow that caught fire and sank following a maritime security incident, and a tanker struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

In recent weeks, Iran has reported multiple vessels striking sea mines, prompting US Central Command (CENTCOM), which runs military operations in the region, to reaffirm on social media its insistence that all mines in "primary transit routes" have been cleared.
On Thursday, Hossein Mohebi, the spokesman for the IRGC challenged the claim, saying on X: "Prove your Hormuz mine-clearing claim with independent evidence, not statements!"
Since the outbreak of the war on Feb 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait. On Sunday CENTCOM said it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran considers ships using the southern corridor near the Omani coast unauthorised.

In their statement on Thursday, the Guards said "the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM's delusions on social media".
The IRGC also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone, in a separate statement.
"The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz," the statement said.

9945a3df935f744f: TOLEDO: Spain began demanding answers on Thursday after its second high-speed train collision this year killed 69 people and injured scores, as distraught relatives desperately sought news about their loved ones.

One of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century struck south of Madrid on Wednesday morning when a service operated by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo.
Manuel San Emeterio, whose 54-year-old brother Pepe is missing, travelled to the central city of Toledo to provide DNA samples to the Civil Guard.
"The uncertainty is the worst thing that you deal with, everyone is dealing with it," he said. "But I think there's something that counters it, which is hope... we must never lose it."
Toledo has received 52 of the bodies, overwhelming its morgue's capacity of 30 and forcing the army to set up an improvised facility.
Forensics experts in green jackets, a black funeral car and army vehicles moved in and out of the site, equipped with red marquees and refrigerated containers, an AFP reporter saw.
Sniffer dogs and thermal drones were searching for bodies at the crash site outside the central village of Urda, about 130km south of Madrid.
The death toll rose from 68 to 69 on Thursday, according to regional authorities. Among the victims was Fatima Banez, a former labour minister for the main conservative Popular Party (PP).
'Nervous and desperate' relatives
Jose Miguel Fernandez, a parish priest in Urda, joined emergency services in offering support to families still waiting to learn the fate of their loved ones.
"Many of them were calm, others were nervous and desperate. They wanted to know straight away and get news" of their loved ones, he told AFP.
Flags flew at half-mast on public buildings, while official ceremonies and public events were cancelled or scaled back on the first of three days of national mourning.
A minute's silence was observed across the country, including at Spain's busiest train station, Atocha in Madrid, where some mourners shed tears.
Wednesday's accident happened on a key line linking Madrid to the southern city of Seville, which was also the scene of a collision in January that killed 46 people.
It has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain's high-speed rail network, the second-largest in the world after China's.
Toledo resident Marcos Ibanez, who works in tourism, told AFP he had avoided high-speed trains "for a long time because of this".
"I've gone through the place where the accident happened several times... and you never know when it might be your turn," the 28-year-old said. "Most people are pretty fed up."

During a visit to the disaster site, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faces a general election on Nov 29, pledged "to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again".
King Felipe VI also intervened in the debate after visiting the injured in Toledo, calling for measures "to ensure this does not happen again".
'Searching for culprits'
Transport Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday that an automatic control system had gone down along 69km of track, causing all trains there to be stopped.
But the control centre decided to "resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable", Puente said, with the Renfe train travelling 25km before striking the Iryo.
The control centre "had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it", he added.
Sanchez's main rival, PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo, accused Puente of "frivolity" by trying to pin the blame on one control centre operator.
"Political responsibilities cannot wait for an investigation," Feijoo said.
The head of train driver union Semaf, Diego Martin, said "attention is wrongly being focused on searching for culprits" when workers were using "degraded systems".
Renfe train drivers on Thursday maintained a strike that Semaf had called before the accident "to defend rail safety", saying previous commitments on the issue had been broken.
Renfe reported "a major impact" on its minimum service requirements, with 26.6 per cent of the staff concerned joining the industrial action.
The Madrid region's sprawling commuter network suffered the most disruption, with 81 per cent of its planned services cancelled.

537e938dbc99a7b0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Differing views or approaches among ministries do not necessarily reflect division within the government, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Instead, Anwar described such differences as part of healthy policy deliberations and discussions that take into account respective responsibilities, jurisdictions, and priorities to ensure the effective implementation of the Madani Government’s agenda.

“To ensure effective governance, every government policy and decision must undergo proper deliberation and coordination.

“Matters requiring a collective decision will be tabled for Cabinet consideration and approval, in line with the principle of collective ministerial responsibility,” said Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister.
He said this in a written reply published on the Parliament website yesterday in response to a question from Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin (PN-Larut).
Hamzah had asked about recent instances where the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development publicly issued conflicting positions on several issues.

Anwar gave an assurance that the government will continue to strengthen inter-ministerial cooperation, enhance policy implementation, and monitor initiative outcomes to ensure decisions translate into tangible and sustainable benefits for the people.

The Prime Minister added that the country’s economic performance is monitored continuously based on current indicators to assess policy effectiveness and strengthen economic resilience against global uncertainties. — Bernama
e8942cfadb2641d9: PETALING JAYA: Forget the usual shopping trips and beach holidays. Malaysians appear to be widening their travel horizons, with destinations offering mountain adventures, ancient temples and cultural discoveries attracting growing attention.

From the snow-capped peaks surrounding Almaty in Kazakhstan to the centuries-old wonders of Borobudur in Indonesia, travellers are apparently showing interest in experiences that go beyond conventional holiday itineraries.
According to Traveloka's Southeast Asia Index released earlier this month, searches from Malaysia for Almaty surged 106% year-on-year during the third quarter of the year.
Meanwhile, accommodation bookings from Malaysia to the Indonesian destinations of Magelang and Yogyakarta also increased, reflecting growing interest in the region's celebrated cultural landmarks.
The findings, based on the travel platform's booking and search data between July and September, offer a glimpse of destinations capturing Malaysians' imagination.
Almaty: A mountain escape with a difference
Nestled at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau mountains, Almaty offers scenery that feels worlds apart from Malaysia's tropical landscapes.
Kazakhstan's former capital combines leafy boulevards, lively cafés and cultural attractions with easy access to spectacular natural surroundings.
Just outside the city, visitors can explore the mountainous landscapes of Ile-Alatau National Park, while the turquoise waters of Big Almaty Lake make for a memorable excursion.
Those seeking winter adventures can head to Shymbulak, a mountain resort known for skiing and snowboarding, while the Medeu high-altitude skating rink is another popular attraction.
Almaty's appeal also extends to its markets, museums and food culture, where Central Asian traditions mingle with Russian and other regional influences.
The destination comes with another advantage: Malaysian passport holders can visit Kazakhstan visa-free for up to 30 days.
Java: Where history comes alive
Closer to home, Indonesia's Central Java offers a different kind of adventure, one shaped by ancient civilisations, religious traditions and remarkable architecture.
Traveloka reported growing accommodation bookings from Malaysia to Magelang and Yogyakarta, two destinations associated with some of Indonesia's most celebrated historical sites.

Near Magelang stands Borobudur, one of the world's greatest Buddhist monuments and a Unesco World Heritage Site. Built during the eighth and ninth centuries, the massive stone structure features tiered terraces, intricate relief carvings and 72 perforated stupas containing Buddha statues.
Its architecture reflects Buddhist cosmology, turning a walk through the monument into a journey rich with religious and philosophical meaning.

Not far from Yogyakarta lies another Unesco-listed treasure: Prambanan, Indonesia's largest temple complex dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. Its towering spires and elaborate stone carvings, including scenes from the Ramayana epic, provide a striking contrast to Borobudur's Buddhist architecture.

Beyond the temples, visitors can discover Yogyakarta's traditional batik workshops, bustling markets and Javanese performing arts, making the region an appealing destination for those who enjoy combining sightseeing with cultural experiences.

Of course, travellers should keep an eye on local conditions, as Yogyakarta and parts of Central Java remain unusually dry and susceptible to wildfires ahead of a delayed rainy season, even though widespread haze is currently more concentrated elsewhere in Indonesia.
d03d0b1d9a60bd88: PETALING JAYA: Belanjawan 2027 menurunkan kadar cukai pendapatan korporat perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS) kepada 14% dan 16%, selain meningkatkan kemudahan pinjaman serta jaminan pembiayaan kepada RM57 bilion.
Namun, sejauh mana langkah ini mampu membantu PMKS berkembang dan menjadikan 2027 sebagai 'tahun PMKS Malaysia'?
Pakar ekonomi dan wakil industri menilai kesan langkah tersebut terhadap aliran tunai, produktiviti serta kemampuan perniagaan tempatan berkembang ke pasaran lebih luas.
Penjimatan cukai jadi modal kerja

Belanjawan 2027 mencadangkan pengurangan kadar cukai pendapatan korporat PMKS daripada 15% kepada 14% bagi RM150,000 pertama pendapatan bercukai, dan daripada 17% kepada 16% bagi RM450,000 seterusnya.
Langkah itu dianggarkan memberi penjimatan sehingga RM6,000 kepada perniagaan yang layak, dengan kira-kira 300,000 PMKS dijangka menerima manfaat.
Pakar ekonomi Lai Wei Sieng daripada Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia berkata, kadar 14% dan 16% itu adalah yang terendah setakat ini bagi kategori pendapatan bercukai berkenaan.

Presiden Persatuan Perusahaan Kecil dan Sederhana Malaysia (Samenta) William Ng pula berkata, penjimatan itu tidak wajar dipandang kecil kerana wang berkenaan boleh terus digunakan sebagai modal kerja.

“Saya tahu ada pihak memperkecilkan penjimatan RM6,000 itu, tetapi bagi sebuah PMKS, penjimatan cukai ini membolehkan syarikat mengekalkan lebih banyak wang setiap tahun untuk digunakan sebagai modal kerja,” katanya.

Berbanding geran memerlukan permohonan dan penyediaan dokumen, katanya, pengurangan cukai membolehkan syarikat yang layak menyimpan lebih banyak pendapatan, selain menunjukkan kerajaan memahami cabaran aliran tunai mereka.
Jaminan bantu atasi kekurangan cagaran

Menurut SME Corp, pada tahun 2027, sejumlah RM67.9 billion telah diperuntukkan untuk pembangunan PMKS melalui inisiatif dan program yang dapat memberi manfaat secara langsung dan tidak langsung kepada PMKS, tertinggi dalam sejarah, naik daripada RM54.9 bilion pada tahun 2026.
Sebahagian kemudahan itu turut dibuka kepada syarikat bersaiz pertengahan.
Ng berkata banyak perniagaan kecil, khususnya dalam sektor perkhidmatan, sukar mendapatkan pinjaman disebabkan prestasi kewangan yang tidak sekata atau kekurangan cagaran.
Menurutnya, jaminan kredit dapat mengurangkan risiko yang ditanggung bank, sekali gus meningkatkan peluang permohonan pembiayaan diluluskan.
Bagaimanapun, beliau mengingatkan keputusan pinjaman kekal di tangan bank dan pengusaha perlu membantu institusi kewangan memahami operasi serta keperluan pembiayaan perniagaan mereka.
Ruang menyesuaikan kos gaji

Belanjawan 2027 turut mengumumkan kenaikan gaji minimum daripada RM1,700 kepada RM2,000 mulai Jun 2027, dengan PMKS yang mencatatkan hasil jualan di bawah RM50 juta dikecualikan sementara daripada kadar baharu itu bagi memberi ruang menyesuaikan model perniagaan.
Ng berkata, pengecualian itu mengambil kira perbezaan kemampuan antara perniagaan di pusat ekonomi utama dan bandar kecil.
Menurutnya, banyak PMKS di Lembah Klang, Johor Bahru dan Pulau Pinang sudah membayar gaji melebihi RM2,000, sedangkan perniagaan di bandar kecil lazimnya mempunyai hasil dan kadar gaji lebih rendah.

Namun, beliau menegaskan kenaikan gaji tidak dapat dielakkan dan pengusaha perlu memanfaatkan ruang yang diberikan untuk menyesuaikan operasi, termasuk beralih kepada automasi dan pendigitalan bagi mengurangkan kebergantungan kepada tenaga kerja.
Pemodenan bukan lagi pilihan
Bagi pakar ekonomi Tan Peck Leong, sokongan pemodenan antara langkah paling penting dalam Belanjawan 2027 bagi memastikan kelangsungan dan daya saing PMKS.
Belanjawan itu turut menaikkan had nilai aset kecil yang layak mendapat elaun modal kepada RM3,000 dan melanjutkan Elaun Modal Dipercepatkan bagi mesin serta peralatan ICT tertentu hingga akhir 2030.

Selain RM30 juta melalui MDEC untuk membantu 4,000 PMKS menggunakan AI dan automasi, kerajaan menyediakan RM60 juta kepada Matrade dan pembiayaan RM1 bilion melalui BPMB bagi menyokong peluasan pasaran eksport.

Tan berkata pelaburan dalam teknologi membolehkan perniagaan meningkatkan pengeluaran tanpa kenaikan kos pekerja yang terlalu tinggi, tetapi usaha itu mesti disertai pengurusan berkeupayaan dan tenaga kerja mahir.
“Dalam persekitaran persaingan hari ini, pemodenan bukan lagi satu pilihan, tetapi satu keperluan untuk terus bertahan dan berkembang,” katanya.
Bantuan membuka jalan untuk berkembang
Pengalaman beberapa usahawan menunjukkan bagaimana bantuan kerajaan boleh membantu perniagaan berkembang.
Kehilangan pekerjaan ketika pandemik mendorong R Abiramee, ibu kepada tiga anak, memulakan perniagaan ais krim dari rumah.
Geran RM76,000 daripada SME Corp kemudian membantunya membeli tiga mesin penting untuk pengeluaran.
“Kalau hari itu SME Corp tidak beri saya geran, mungkin impian saya tidak akan menjadi kenyataan,” katanya.

Baginya, penjimatan cukai sehingga RM6,000 yang dicadangkan dalam Belanjawan 2027 bukan jumlah kecil kerana wang itu boleh digunakan untuk membeli enam peti sejuk beku bagi restoran yang menjual produknya.

Beliau kini mahu membawa jenama Jumboo Ice Cream ke pasar raya dan akhirnya ke luar negara, tetapi berharap bantuan turut diberikan bagi mengatasi halangan memasuki pasaran lebih besar, termasuk kos penyenaraian produk.
Sementara itu, Meor Tawfik daripada Ventura IoT pernah berdepan projek tertangguh dan bayaran pelanggan tersekat ketika pandemik sehingga terpaksa berbincang dengan pekerja mengenai pengurangan gaji.
Selepas pandemik, geran SME Corp membantu syarikatnya menyediakan peralatan demonstrasi mudah alih bagi meyakinkan pelanggan mengenai teknologi penderiaan gentian optiknya.
Peralatan itu turut dibawa ke Indonesia, Thailand dan Vietnam, membolehkan pelanggan melihat sendiri bagaimana teknologi berkenaan berfungsi.
“Kita dapat projek bukan setakat di Malaysia, kita juga dapat projek dari luar negara,” katanya.
Syarikat yang bermula dengan empat pekerja itu kini mempunyai 40 kakitangan, separuh daripadanya jurutera.
Ukuran sebenar ‘tahun PMKS’

Tan berkata kejayaan usaha menjadikan 2027 sebagai 'tahun PMKS Malaysia' tidak seharusnya diukur berdasarkan jumlah bantuan atau bilangan perniagaan baharu semata-mata, sebaliknya pada kemampuan perusahaan sedia ada untuk bertahan dan berkembang seperti yang dilalui Abiramee dan Meor.
Menurutnya, pertumbuhan jualan, peningkatan produktiviti dan kemampuan menembusi pasaran antarabangsa juga perlu dijadikan ukuran.

960d483b0fb80fe2: PETALING JAYA: The 2027 budget cuts corporate tax rates for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to 14% and 16%, while increasing financing facilities and guarantees to help businesses grow.
But to what extent will these measures be enough to make 2027 “the year of Malaysian MSMEs”?
Economists and industry representatives assess the impact of the measures on cash flow, productivity, and local businesses’ ability to expand into wider markets.
Tax savings provide working capital
The 2027 budget proposes reducing corporate tax from 15% to 14% on the first RM150,000 of chargeable income, and from 17% to 16% on the next RM450,000.
The move is expected to save eligible businesses up to RM6,000, benefitting about 300,000 MSMEs.
Economist Lai Wei Sieng of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia said the proposed rates were the lowest for these income brackets to date.

Malaysian Small and Medium Enterprises Association (Samenta) president William Ng said the savings should not be dismissed as insignificant, as the money could be put directly towards working capital.
“I know some people have played down the RM6,000 in savings, but for an MSME, these tax savings allow a company to retain more money each year for working capital,” he said.
Ng said that unlike grants, which require applications and documentation, tax cuts allow eligible companies to retain more of their earnings.
He said the move also showed that the government understood the cash flow challenges businesses faced.
Guarantees help overcome collateral constraints

According to SME Corp, RM67.9 billion had been allocated for MSME development in 2027 through initiatives and programmes that could benefit these businesses directly and indirectly, the highest amount on record, up from RM54.9 billion in 2026.
Some financing facilities are also available to mid-sized companies.
Ng said many small businesses, particularly in the services sector, struggled to obtain loans because of inconsistent financial performance or a lack of collateral.
Credit guarantees can reduce banks’ risks and improve businesses’ chances of securing financing, he said.
However, he cautioned that lending decisions remained with the banks, and business owners needed to help financial institutions understand their operations and financing needs.
Room to adjust wage costs
The 2027 budget also sees the minimum wage raised from RM1,700 to RM2,000 from June next year. MSMEs with annual sales below RM50 million will be temporarily exempted to give them time to adjust.
Ng said the exemption recognised that businesses in major cities generally had greater financial capacity than those in smaller towns.
Many MSMEs in the Klang Valley, Johor Bahru and Penang already paid wages above RM2,000, while businesses in smaller towns tended to have lower revenue and wage levels, he said.

Ng stressed that wage increases were inevitable and business owners should use the time provided to adjust their operations, including by adopting automation and digitalisation to reduce their reliance on labour.
Modernisation no longer optional
Economist Tan Peck Leong said support for modernisation was among the most important measures in Budget 2027 to ensure MSMEs remained viable and competitive.

The budget also raises the threshold for small-value assets eligible for capital allowances to RM3,000 and extends accelerated capital allowances for certain ICT machinery and equipment until the end of 2030.
The government has also allocated RM30 million through the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation to help 4,000 MSMEs adopt AI and automation.

Another RM60 million has been allocated to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, while Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd will provide RM1 billion in financing to help businesses expand into export markets.
Tan said investing in technology could help businesses increase production without sharply raising labour costs, but such efforts had to be accompanied by capable management and a skilled workforce.
“In today's competitive environment, modernisation is no longer an option, but a necessity to survive and grow,” he said.
Assistance opens the door to growth
The experiences of two entrepreneurs show how government assistance can help businesses grow.
R Abiramee started making ice cream from home after losing her job during the pandemic. A RM76,000 grant from SME Corp later helped her buy three production machines.
“If SME Corp had not given me the grant then, my dream might never have become a reality,” she said.
For Abiramee, the proposed tax savings of up to RM6,000 were far from insignificant, as the money saved could be used to buy six freezers for restaurants selling her Jumboo Ice Cream products.
Abiramee hopes to get her products into supermarkets and eventually overseas. However, she said more help was needed to overcome barriers to entering bigger markets, including product listing fees.
Meor Tawfik of Ventura IoT also received help from SME Corp after his business struggled with project delays and late payments during the pandemic.
The grant helped his company develop portable demonstration equipment for its fibre-optic sensing technology, allowing potential customers to see how it worked.
The equipment was also taken to Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam, allowing potential customers to see how the technology worked.
“We secured projects not just in Malaysia, but also overseas,” he said.
Ventura IoT has since grown from four employees to 40, half of whom are engineers.
What would make 2027 a success?
Tan said the success of efforts to make 2027 the year of Malaysian MSMEs should not be measured by the amount of aid distributed or the number of new businesses established.
Instead, the focus should be on whether existing businesses could survive, grow and become more productive.
Sales growth and the ability to enter international markets should also be used to measure progress, he said.
“We want to see more micro enterprises grow into small enterprises, and small enterprises grow into medium-sized enterprises,” he said.

7c2ff26b5479225f: LONDON: Sergio Garcia will target an 11th Ryder Cup appearance in Ireland next year after he became the latest leading golfer to confirm he was leaving the struggling LIV Golf circuit.
The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy protection.
But that has not stopped several players from announcing their intention to return to the established US PGA and European circuits.

European players such as Garcia have also been told signing with the new-look LIV will make them ineligible for European tour membership and so rule them out of the Ryder Cup – the biennial team event against the United States.
Garcia is also the all-time leading points scorer in Ryder Cup history, with the 46-year-old Spaniard having amassed 28.5 points in 10 appearances.

In an X post on Thursday, the 2017 US Masters champion also referenced his conduct at Augusta National this year, where he was issued with a code-of-conduct warning after he broke his driver on the second hole.
"This off-season, I'm working really hard on my game and putting a big focus on a strong mindset and my mental health," said Garcia.
"Next season, I'll be playing on the DP World (European) Tour. This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again.
"I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour."
Garcia added: "I left Augusta last year disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally.

"Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place... Another goal is to make that Ryder Cup team and to be an asset to the guys in whatever capacity that may be. In golf, everything is earned and nothing is given. Let's get to work."

LIV's future is uncertain after it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States following the withdrawal of financial support from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, their longtime backers.

Last week, England's Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton both announced they were leaving LIV, even though new lead investor BC Partners Credit has pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential US$300 million to help the circuit relaunch in 2027.
Earlier this month, two-time major champion Jon Rahm reached a separation agreement with LIV.

Rahm was LIV's largest unsecured creditor with US$7.5 million owed when LIV filed for bankruptcy. The 31-year-old Spaniard was thought to have been owed much more after signing a deal worth a reported US$300 million to leave the PGA Tour for LIV in December 2023. — AFP
259334bbd452616d: MEXICO CITY: George Russell said one difficult Formula One season would not define his career and he still had plenty of time on his side.
The Briton started the campaign as the favourite but has been eclipsed by 20-year-old Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, who is set to clinch the title in Mexico City this weekend.

"I've probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked, in all honesty," Russell said on Thursday, acknowledging that Antonelli, who will be Italy's first champion in 73 years, had been performing at a higher level.

"But I remind myself I'm 28 years old. I see Lewis (Hamilton) still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando (Alonso) at 44. Lewis won the majority of his titles in his 30s, and this year is absolutely not going to define my career as a whole."
Ferrari's Hamilton is third in the standings, one point behind Russell.
While Antonelli has won 9 of 18 grands prix this season, Russell has 3 to his credit and his season has been characterised by misfortune, with highs one weekend and lows the next.
He said also that his natural driving style had been hampered by "a few factors" involving the new era of power units and higher tyre pressures, especially on the rear of the car.
"It's not going to break me. If anything, it's going to make me stronger. I've been pretty proud of my resilience and how I've bounced back from very tough moments," he said.
"Through my lowest points of this season, I've generally bounced back really, really strong. Then I had another bad race after the good one.

"But I've been racing more years of my life than I haven't, and I've had more successful years than relative failures ... unfortunately, this year for me has come at maybe the time when I needed it most (to be at the highest level), but it's by no means the end of my journey. I've still got a good 12 to 15 years left in me."
Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff has expressed his confidence in Russell bouncing back, saying the current car did not suit the driver but next year would be a fresh start.
d4a0d21f16918ace: TOKYO: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to keep interest rates steady on Friday but stress its focus on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its two per cent target, suggesting scope to raise borrowing costs as soon as December.
Such guidance would reinforce the central bank's message last month that it has entered a new, more hawkish policy phase and is open to raising rates once every few months, analysts said.

The shift would also align the BOJ with its US and European counterparts, which are eyeing near-term rate hikes to tackle inflationary risks from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom and the energy shock triggered by the Iran war.

"Global price pressures from AI investment are quite strong, which means the recent inflation is partly demand driven," said Kazuo Momma, a former BOJ executive who is currently executive economist at Mizuho Research Institute.
"By declaring that its policy phase has changed, the BOJ is essentially telling markets it will hike rates once a quarter," he said, predicting rate hikes in December and March next year.

At the two-day meeting ending on Friday, the BOJ is expected to maintain its policy rate at 1.25 per cent, foregoing a back-to-back hike to allow more time to scrutinise the impact of previous rate increases on lending conditions.

In its quarterly report, the BOJ is likely to slightly revise upwards its price forecast for the next financial year and signal that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2 per cent target, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

With wage gains becoming embedded and inflation expectations hovering around two per cent, the central bank is likely to stress that it will now focus on anchoring inflation around its target by raising rates towards levels deemed neutral to the economy.
Markets will scrutinise comments from Governor Kazuo Ueda's post-meeting news conference for clues on the pace and timing of further rate hikes.

"If the BOJ were to say underlying inflation reached levels consistent with its two per cent price target, that would have important policy implications," said former BOJ official Nobuyasu Atago, who is currently chief economist at Rakuten Securities Economic Research Institute.
"It would be a show of resolve the BOJ won't tolerate any further overshoot in inflation," and signal the possibility of more nimble rate hikes next year, he said.

With persistently high energy costs and rising import prices due to a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ raised rates in September after delivering an increase in June, a shorter interval than the roughly twice-yearly hikes in 2024 and 2025.

Most analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent in December, followed by further increases next year. Their projections for the terminal rate centre around 1.75 to two per cent.

Annual core inflation in Tokyo, seen as a leading indicator of nationwide price trends, exceeded the central bank's two per cent target by a wide margin in October, data showed on Friday, highlighting mounting price pressures.
Rising prices could weigh on consumption as they prompt Japanese households, many of whom have never experienced widespread price increases in their lifetime, to seek discounts.
In its latest quarterly projections in July, the BOJ expected consumer inflation to accelerate in the coming months as firms continued to pass on rising costs.
ff07e5548858aeb8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Mention Teochew cuisine and what comes to mind are usually these three dishes: Teochew porridge, braised duck or the light and clean flavours of Teochew steamed fish accentuated by sour plums, ginger and tomatoes.
Enter Teochew House: a casual offshoot of the posh Upper Palace Teochew located in The Exchange TRX that offers a different perspective of the cuisine.

The restaurant at Steppes continues Upper Palace Teochew’s mission to champion the finer details of the cuisine, offering staples like noodles served with braised beef and tendons, fish balls, prawn wantans and rice bowls with braised pork trotters or braised goose for quick lunch breaks or family-style meals for leisurely dinners.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
When they get it right, the Pan-fried Teochew Oyster Omelette is a crispy, golden wonder with its light crust, oysters and greens.
On paper, separate menus exist for lunch and dinner, though some favourites overlap. You can also add items from the extensive dinner menu to your lunch order.

There’s also a secret menu, known only to regulars, where you can order the freshest catch delivered daily, whether it’s a particular type of fish cooked to your preference or even crabs to enhance your porridge’s sweetness.

You can’t go wrong ordering the Teochew Oyster Porridge (RM38.80), which diners love for its soupy porridge with soft whole rice grains mingling with plump oysters, minced pork, sliced mushrooms, preserved radish, greens and dried prawns.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Sweet and Sour Pork with Pineapple was a surprise hit that must be eaten immediately after it hits the table.

For the Teochews, the familiar, simple flavours are reminiscent of home cooking, which they recognise immediately, while non-Teochews appreciate the warmth of the sweet, clear broth and fluffy grains that can be eaten with other dishes.
Pan-fried Teochew Oyster Omelette (RM32.80) can be seen on almost every table, resembling a pizza that servers cut into wedges using stainless steel pizza wheels.
A layer of puffy crispy egg with a light crunch hides plump oysters and chopped greens cradled in the fluffy cooked eggs.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Steamed Pork Patty with Preserved Radish is the quintessential comfort food best paired with rice.
On a good day when the kitchen isn’t overwhelmed, you get a beautiful golden filigree crust dotted with chopped greens as juicy oysters peek through.

During peak hours, however, there’s a possibility of getting a dud — an over-fried omelette with hard oysters — which we encountered during a weekend dinner. Hopefully the kitchen can eliminate these uncertainties over time.

You may think we were mad to order classic dishes like Sweet and Sour Pork with Pineapple (RM58) and Steamed Pork Patty with Preserved Radish (RM58) instead of more Teochew-style dishes but there’s an important Hong Kong connection: Upper Palace Teochew partnered with Hung’s Delicacies from Hong Kong to introduce these items on the menu.
So we took a chance when we saw them on Teochew House’s menu. Our guess hit the bullseye; the sweet and sour pork was superb and definitely ranks as one of the best in town.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Chicken and Pork Soup with Hairy Fig (left) has a sweet coconut-like aroma. Teochew Marinated Raw Sea Prawns (right) preserves the prawns with soy sauce, Shao Xing rice wine and spices.
Eat each nugget the moment it hits the table as inside the light crust, you get layers of pork rolled that are juicy as you chew on it.
The pork patty was also good, offering a soft, fluffy texture because of its high fat-to-meat ratio, peppered with chunks of water chestnut and topped with preserved olive leaves.
Chicken and Pork Soup with Hairy Fig (RM88) was another big surprise; a friend who had tried hairy fig root before insisted we order this for dinner.
That became a stealth winner as the hairy fig root imparts a sweet coconut-like aroma to the silky broth.
Don’t ignore the soup’s dregs either, as they aren’t dried out but remain juicy and infused with the herbs’ flavour, making us fight for the chicken meat.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Braised Lion-Head Goose Meat uses a master braising stock of spices and soy sauce.
The Teochews are experts at handling seafood, which includes curing it Sheng Yan style to enhance the seafood’s texture and sweetness.

Teochew Marinated Raw Sea Prawns (RM38) is a fine example of the method where tiger prawns are infused in Shao Xing wine, soy sauce, garlic, Sichuan peppercorns, coriander and other spices until they achieve a firmer texture infused with the marinade’s flavours.

The traditional braised items use goose meat, web and wings, various parts of the pig — from its jowl, belly to its ears and intestines — and cuttlefish, braised in a master stock rich with soy sauce and infused with spices
A special breed of goose, known as the Lion Head or Shitou, is used, as it is prized for its rich, flavourful meat, head, and liver.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Teochew Yam Paste with Gingko Beans (left) has smooth yam paste served without lard. Freshly Ground Almond Cream with Egg White (right) is the best dessert choice.
Braised Lion-Head Goose Meat (RM58.80) has a deeper flavour from the spices and tender meat while the Braised Pork Jowl (RM38.80) has more bite and is paired with a lighter stock.
For lunch, the Pork Trotter Rice (RM32.80) is served in a bowl where the soft, tender meat accompanies rice drenched in the braising liquid.

For a complete meal, an assortment of greens with different textures was added to the table like the crunchier Stir-fried French Bean with Minced Pork & Preserved Olive (RM32) and a softer Baby Cabbage in Rich Chicken Broth (RM33).
Dessert choices are limited to only three items.
The classic Teochew Yam Paste with Gingko Beans (RM12.80) has an enjoyable smoothness but without the essential lard for flavour and a silkier mouthfeel, it feels like a cheat dessert.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Teochew House is a welcome addition to the Mont Kiara neighbourhood.
On the healthier side, the Water Chestnut and Mung Bean Sweet Soup (RM10.80) is extremely light in sweetness, containing only mung beans and showing no sign of any crunch from water chestnuts.
At the end of the day, Freshly Ground Almond Cream with Egg White (RM15.80) won the sweet battle with its light but distinct flavour of Chinese almonds and ribbons of cooked egg white.
Bookings, especially during peak times, are needed to score a coveted table. It’s also best to pre-book items for faster dish turnaround.
Teochew House
G-05-01, Steppes,
No. 32, Jalan Kiara 3,
Mont Kiara, Kuala Lumpur.
Open daily: 11am to 3pm, 5.30pm to 10pm
*This is an independent review where the writer paid for the meal.

145ed64c45a52c9c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz has poked fun at Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, asking whether he was more nervous about exchanging wedding vows with actress Bella Astillah or signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the government.

“One is a promise to build a future together with a partner, while the other is a commitment to the future of Muar residents,” he wrote.
The post followed the Madani government’s signing of an MoU with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) and several other opposition MPs, including Syed Saddiq.

Tengku Zafrul, who is also Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s senior political adviser, said the MPs would remain in the opposition despite agreeing to support the Budget and key institutional reforms.
He added that their respective constituencies would receive equivalent allocations for the benefit of the people.
“In politics, we do not necessarily have to agree on everything. But when it comes to the interests of the people, we must be able to work together,” he said.
The post was accompanied by the hashtags #TZA and #MadaniBekerja.

aedd41ab24e776d5: LIVERPOOL: David Moyes pointedly praised Everton's "really good values" after Jack Grealish was dropped for breaching club discipline prior to Thursday's 3-1 win over Newcastle in the League Cup.
Grealish reportedly skipped training ahead of the fourth round tie and was left out of the Everton squad at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
The on-loan Manchester City winger had missed Everton's defeat at Arsenal in the Premier League on Saturday due to illness.
Everton boss Moyes refused to give further details on Grealish's absence against Newcastle, but backed the move to leave him out.
"It was a club decision. I support the decision. It's something I don't really want to speak too much about," he said.

Asked about the response of his players on a night when the controversy could have been a distraction, Moyes's answer suggested frustration with Grealish, who has repeatedly been criticised for his off-field behaviour.
England international Grealish fell out of favour at City after several late-night incidents and reports of after-hours drinking.
"I think the one thing about Everton and what they've got is they've got really good values behind it," Moyes said.
"All the players stand up to the values, accept the values that we put out there, what we want from them on the pitch and off the pitch.
"And from that point of view I think the players have done a brilliant job tonight, they really did."
Everton took control of the game in the first half with goals from James Garner and Hayden Hackney before Thierno Barry ended any doubt in the 69th minute.
Dan Burn scored a late goal for Newcastle but Everton eased through to face fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the quarter-finals in December.
Fleetwood stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday, but Everton will fancy their chances of making the semi-finals of a competition they have never won.
Everton have not lifted a major trophy since the 1995 FA Cup.
"I think the minute you use the word quarter-finals then you start to think, 'this sounds good'," Moyes said.
"I think we're pleased that we've been able to get to this stage of the competition. If we can keep it going great, obviously."
92b9f76eda8d0dd4: MAX VERSTAPPEN said a future Le Mans entry with former Red Bull teammate Daniel Ricciardo could appeal, but only if it came with the preparation needed to properly challenge for victory.

Ricciardo raised the prospect on Wednesday on Formula One's "Beyond The Grid" podcast, saying he could consider a one-off return to racing at the 24 Hours of Le Mans rather than a full-season comeback.
Asked about a preferred teammate, the Australian named Verstappen, whom he raced with at Red Bull from 2016 to 2018, as a leading candidate.
"He's a smart man to choose me in the car," Verstappen told reporters on Thursday at the Mexican Grand Prix.
The Dutchman added, however, that his Formula One commitments and projects away from the championship left little space in his calendar for endurance racing.
"If I want to do it, I want to do it properly, with really good prep," Verstappen said. "At the moment I cannot do that. I don't have the time, the free time, to dedicate to a Le Mans project."

"If we do something like that, it needs to be proper. It needs to be for a chance to win," he added. "To have a chance to win against people who do it the whole season, you need to be prepared really well."
For now, Verstappen's attention is on a demanding weekend at the high altitude of Mexico City's Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

"With the altitude, normally we have the wings to compensate a little bit for that, but now you basically just run one wing," he said. "So there will be a lot less downforce on the car, which I think will already be quite challenging." — REUTERS

379ef5101637b91c: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit open higher for 10 consecutive trading days against the US dollar on Friday, reflecting continued positive sentiment in the local currency at the start of trading.
At 8am, the ringgit edged up to 4.0570/0625 against the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0575/0620.
The currency was trading near a seven-week high, with its previous opening level of 4.0560 recorded on Sept 9, 2026.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.33 per cent to 101.854 points.

He said the decline came despite better-than-expected US gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026) and a higher personal consumption expenditure (PCE) inflation rate in September.
Mohd Afzanizam said the two-year and 10-year US Treasury yields also fell by 10 and eight basis points to 4.60 per cent and 4.94 per cent, respectively.
"Hence, we believe the market is pricing in the possibility that the Federal Reserve (Fed) might change its direction on monetary policy.

"As such, the ringgit is likely to maintain its positive trend in the near term, given the limited scope for further Fed monetary tightening. The ringgit-US dollar pair could therefore hover between RM4.05 and RM4.07 today," he told Bernama.
Against other major currencies, the ringgit traded lower at the opening.
It weakened against the British pound to 5.4275/4348 from 5.4009/4069 at Thursday's close, and slipped against the euro to 4.5365/5427 from 4.5176/5226.
It also edged lower against the Japanese yen to 2.5707/5743 from 2.5685/5715 previously.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit traded mixed.
It was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 223.6/224.0 from 223.7/224.0 at Thursday's close, and remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.35/6.36.
Meanwhile, the ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1700/1746 from 3.1665/1702 at Thursday's close, and slipped against the Thai baht to 12.0279/0513 from 12.0165/0345.

7151e1f338f826df: LOS ANGELES, Oct 29 — Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the Star Trek and X-Men franchises, has died at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86.
His death on Wednesday came after a “brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.
“His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said.

The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre in London, and worked on British television.

But he rocketed into the pop culture history books in his mid-40s when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, and then again as Professor Charles Xavier in multiple X-Men and related Marvel films.

“He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise,” the official statement said.
Aboard the Enterprise
Stewart was 47 when he debuted as Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, the first live-action television spinoff of the trailblazing sci-fi series from the late 1960s.
He effectively filled the boots of William Shatner’s Captain Kirk from the original show—to resounding success, both in the TV series and in several films.
Picard became known for a few catchphrases including “Make it so” and “Engage!”
But his move to America in 1987 was initially greeted with disdain by the Los Angeles Times, who wrote him off as an “unknown British Shakespearean actor.”
Stewart later dubbed suggestions he was “slumming it” by moving into US television offensive.
He once called his Shakespearean bona fides “nothing but a preparation for sitting in the captain’s chair of the Enterprise.”
Colossus of both stage and screen
Stewart found further acclaim in many films of the X-Men series, debuting in 2000 as Professor Charles Xavier, the founder and mentor of the mutant superhero team.
“For more than 25 years, he brought a gravitas and profundity to the role, earning fans across the globe,” Marvel Studios said yesterday.
Longtime co-star Hugh Jackman, who played Wolverine, remembered Stewart as both “one of the greats of stage and screen” and “a tremendous friend and man.”
Stewart is to make his final on-screen film appearance as Professor Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday, set for release in December.
“What a heartbreaking week it has been,” posted Shatner.
Stewart’s death marked the second in days from the Star Trek universe, following that of Walter Koenig, who played Chekov in the original series.
Shatner said Stewart—who most recently played Picard in 2023 — brought “intelligence, grace and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.”
Stewart earned four Emmy nominations but never won. He did nab a spoken word Grammy, for his narration of Prokofiev: Peter And The Wolf.
And even as he found success in Hollywood, Stewart’s love of theater, and the bard in particular, never left him.
Between filming, he would return to the stage, winning two Olivier awards.
Shakespeare, Stewart said, “feels like a friend, someone who just went out of the room to get another bottle of wine.”
The Royal Shakespeare Company called him “a colossus of both stage and screen and one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation.”
Troubled start
Stewart was born on July 13, 1940 in the small West Yorkshire town of Mirfield, the third of three brothers in a working-class family.

His father, back from World War II and perhaps suffering from PTSD, would often beat Stewart’s mother—which prompted Stewart to later work with the charity Refuge, which specializes in domestic abuse.
The actor left school at 15, and studied at Bristol Old Vic Drama School beginning in 1957, making his professional acting debut two years later.
Prematurely balding, Stewart missed out on many of the young romantic leads but quickly slotted into theater life, joining the RSC in 1966 and staying there until 1982.
Any misgivings Stewart had about taking the Picard role in the “Star Trek” universe were mollified by the thought it would be a one-season failure.
He was wrong.
“It changed my life,” he said.

Knighted in 2010, Stewart married three times: to Sheila Falconer, with whom he had two children; briefly to Star Trek producer Wendy Neuss; and most recently to American singer Sunny Ozell, 38 years his junior. — AFP

The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week's updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.

He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday's new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe.
Due to a knee injury the Italian Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him.

Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain's Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books.

The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German's racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction.
But once the umpire covered up the problematic panel with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve.

The Spaniard will next meet American Tommy Paul for a spot in the semi-finals.
Another former top-ranked player in Russia's Daniil Medvedev also enjoyed success as he battled past Britain's Cameron Norrie in three sets. — AFP
